In today's world, technology enables individuals to accomplish numerous activities without direct interaction with others. People can borrow books, make purchases, and enjoy entertainment without speaking to anyone face to face. The question of whether this reduction in human contact brought about by technology has positive or negative consequences remains relevant. I am convinced that technology has beneficial effects on people's lives because it allows us to communicate with distant individuals, work remotely without commuting, and discover new connections across the globe.

The first reason why technology is advantageous relates to maintaining relationships with family and friends who live far away. When we feel homesick or want to share important news, we can simply make a video call and see each other's faces in real time. Without modern technology, staying in touch with loved ones who reside in different countries would be extremely difficult. There is a possibility that we might gradually lose connection with them over time. Additionally, technology provides safety benefits. If an emergency occurs, family members can locate us quickly using our devices. Moreover, when illness prevents us from going to work, we can telephone our supervisor to inform them of our situation, which would be impossible without technological devices.

The second reason concerns the opportunity to work online from home. This approach offers significant advantages as it eliminates the need for daily commuting, saving both time and transportation costs. For parents, this arrangement is particularly valuable since they can fulfill their professional responsibilities while remaining present for their children. Individuals who are unable to drive also benefit greatly because remote work allows them to earn income without traveling long distances. Furthermore, those who enjoy traveling can continue working while abroad, effectively combining leisure with productivity and increasing their earnings.

The third reason involves the ability to encounter new people, cultures, and languages through technology. Social media platforms connect us with individuals from diverse backgrounds, enabling us to learn about their traditions and customs. We can communicate with them directly and ask questions about their countries, religions, and way of life. Technology also proves invaluable when navigating unfamiliar places. When visiting a foreign country where we do not speak the language or know anyone, we might easily lose our way. In such situations, translation applications on our phones can help us communicate with locals and ask for assistance.

In conclusion, technology exerts a positive influence on our daily lives by providing countless useful functions. It serves as a powerful tool that assists us with nearly everything we need to accomplish in the modern world.

In today's educational landscape, schools increasingly offer opportunities for students to explore their creative talents through various arts programs. These classes provide valuable chances for young people to discover their natural abilities while also serving as a much-needed break from academic pressure. After spending several hours focused on traditional subjects, students often feel mentally exhausted and benefit greatly from activities that allow them to unwind and recharge their energy for the next learning session.

Many high school students find their regular studies monotonous and struggle to identify their true interests within the conventional curriculum. In such situations, engaging in artistic activities becomes an effective solution to combat boredom and refresh the mind. Whether it involves joining a musical band, participating in drama productions, or attending art classes, these opportunities motivate students and make their overall school experience more enjoyable. Schools should therefore ensure these options remain accessible to all learners.

Furthermore, creative subjects play a crucial role in mental relaxation. After intensive study sessions filled with new information, students need activities that help clear their minds and prepare them for continued learning. When students engage in singing, acting, or painting, their brains experience necessary rest, which actually enhances their capacity to absorb subsequent information. This relaxation effect depends on individual preferences, as different students find different artistic outlets most calming and beneficial.

However, while arts education offers numerous advantages, requiring all students to participate in these classes could create problems. Students who lack genuine interest in music, drama, or visual arts might disrupt the learning environment for others. They could become disengaged, fall asleep, or create noise that negatively affects classmates who genuinely want to participate. For this reason, arts classes should remain elective options rather than mandatory requirements.

In conclusion, schools should definitely provide arts classes because they help students feel refreshed after demanding academic periods, improve their ability to learn new information, and increase motivation while reducing pressure. Nevertheless, these programs work best when students can choose them based on their individual interests and talents. This elective approach ensures that those who genuinely want to develop their artistic abilities can do so without being held back by uninterested peers, while students who prefer other activities are not forced to waste time on subjects that do not appeal to them.

Emerson's quote "unless you try to do something beyond what you already mastered, you will never grow" presents an important idea about personal development. I completely agree with this statement, and I would like to explain my reasons.

My first point is that relying on a single skill or area of knowledge limits our potential. In today's competitive world, people who only master one thing often face fewer opportunities. For instance, someone who has only learned one profession may struggle to find employment if that field becomes less demanding. Without diverse abilities, individuals may find themselves stuck in situations where they cannot adapt or progress. This is why it is essential to prepare ourselves with multiple skills and knowledge areas.

Secondly, having different types of knowledge provides significant advantages in life. Knowledge is perhaps the most powerful tool that humans can possess because it cannot be easily taken away. When we expand our abilities beyond what we already know, we become more valuable in the job market and in society. People who continuously learn and develop new skills tend to have better chances of success. They can adapt to changing circumstances and take advantage of new opportunities that come their way.

Finally, growth only happens when we step outside our comfort zones and attempt more challenging tasks. If we stay with what we already know how to do, we will never discover our full potential. For example, a teacher who decides to pursue further education and become a principal demonstrates this principle perfectly. By taking on a more demanding role, that person grows both professionally and personally.

In conclusion, I strongly agree with Emerson's statement. His words remind us that true growth requires effort and the courage to move beyond our current abilities. Only by challenging ourselves can we reach our full potential and lead fulfilling lives.

Technology has both limitations and benefits when it comes to human interaction. The impact of technology on people's lives can be either positive or negative. Today, technology is present almost everywhere we go. Without it, we would have fewer opportunities to learn and grow. Additionally, people no longer need to meet in person to communicate because advanced technology allows us to stay connected with others across different continents through our phones and computers. Technology makes many tasks easier, and I believe it generally affects our lives in positive ways. Here are some examples to support my view.

Technology serves many purposes in daily life that create beneficial outcomes. For numerous individuals, technology represents their source of income. They can work independently and find answers to their questions without asking others. Without technology, they would struggle to earn a living. Moreover, technology plays a vital role in education. Students frequently complete their assignments on computers and submit them through the internet. When they have questions, they can simply search for information online. In American schools, students and teachers rely heavily on technology, using it for approximately fifty percent of their work. They prefer using technology to find information rather than consulting traditional books. Similarly, doctors depend on advanced technological devices to assist their patients. Many medical tools help them perform life-saving operations, and they now trust technology more than textbooks. Furthermore, factories utilize technology extensively, which reduces the physical burden on workers. Machines now handle tasks that humans once performed manually, such as packaging products.

People can use technology for either good or harmful purposes. Over time, individuals have learned how to utilize technology in various ways. The majority employ technology for constructive purposes, including professionals like secretaries, teachers, and doctors who use it to communicate effectively and store important data. Some parents even rely on technology as a form of entertainment for their children. In Latin American countries, many parents refer to devices like phones and tablets as the "new babysitter" because they keep children occupied while parents attend to other responsibilities. However, some individuals exploit technology for dishonest purposes. They learn how to deceive others or gather personal information through social media platforms. Unfortunately, there are cases where criminals use technology to kidnap people or steal money from bank accounts. Elderly individuals often become victims of online fraud. Additionally, hackers steal account information without considering the consequences for their victims. These examples demonstrate that not everyone uses technology responsibly.

Technology also transforms the way people live and think. On a positive note, advanced technology provides increased security in our homes through various safety devices. Moreover, individuals who enjoy sharing content publicly can build careers on social media platforms. Influencers and YouTubers may not personally know their viewers, yet they regularly communicate with them. Technology has also changed how older generations communicate. In the past, people wrote letters to stay in touch, but now they send text messages or make video calls without meeting in person. This development benefits those who live far apart, as technology enables them to maintain relationships despite geographical distances.

Despite these advantages, the limitation of face-to-face contact sometimes creates problems. At work, employees need to communicate effectively with their colleagues to maintain good working relationships. Similarly, couples cannot rely solely on text messages; they require direct conversation to strengthen their bond. However, there are situations where technology proves beneficial. Students can discuss assignments with classmates through digital platforms or search for answers when they need clarification. In conclusion, both technology and human contact have their advantages and disadvantages. Some people prefer using technology over books because they find reading tedious, though technology does not always provide reliable information. Ultimately, I believe we need more genuine human interaction alongside technological communication.

Online learning and video conferencing provide excellent opportunities for students who cannot afford traditional college education and for older adults who never had the chance to pursue further studies due to financial constraints. Money problems are a significant challenge in today's society, as students need to pay for accommodation whether on or off campus. Many students drop out because they simply cannot afford these expenses. Additionally, most students have part-time jobs to cover their living costs, and balancing work with studies is extremely demanding and stressful.

Transportation and parking present another major difficulty for many learners. Students who attend large campuses often struggle to find parking spaces, and not everyone owns a vehicle. By studying from home, learners can avoid these complications and never worry about being late to class. After a long day, they can start their lessons whenever convenient.

Studying remotely offers numerous advantages regarding concentration and productivity. Students experience fewer distractions at home, which helps them focus better on the material and understand lessons more effectively. They can review recorded lectures as many times as needed until they fully grasp the content. Additionally, teachers often assign less work to online students, giving them more time to manage other responsibilities.

Online education also allows learners to take care of personal matters, arrive on time for sessions, and save money on transportation. It provides opportunities for those who previously had no access to higher education to achieve their dreams while developing better organizational and time management skills.

First, young students often abandon their courses. When teenagers enroll in career-related classes, many give up after just a few weeks. Additionally, adults prefer to spend time with friends and enjoy their youth before focusing on their professional future. Young students are not yet ready to handle such serious decision-making.

In reality, many children would rather spend their time playing video games or enjoying other hobbies than planning for their future. Furthermore, they often do not understand what career planning actually involves. When asked to write about their future profession, many students simply write "don't know" and return to their regular activities. This shows that they are not prepared to make such important decisions.

Similarly, smart people can continue growing or potentially become less honest over time. If no one teaches them to maintain their honesty, they might start lying as they get older.

We tend to be more casual with friends, who might try to lead us into situations where we forget about the importance of being honest. This is why honesty should be the number one priority in everyone's life.

Some people may argue the opposite, but starting with modest goals actually helps identify the small issues that need correction.

Individuals should consider setting their expectations low so they can begin by examining what needs improvement. These are the elements that will ultimately make them stronger and more capable of achieving various things.

Those who begin at the lowest level are often the ones who surpass their own aspirations. They become capable individuals precisely because they set realistic goals and reach milestones along the way. People develop themselves because the mistakes they make during their journey are what help build their character and transform them into stronger, more versatile individuals.

Some individuals aim high believing that by doing so, they will be able to overcome obstacles and solve any problems that arise without putting in real effort or taking time to think things through. People should start somewhat lower than this because that approach allows them to build the foundation and character that will assist them in reaching their objectives through consistent effort, rather than aiming too high and falling short. For instance, someone who declares they will accomplish great things while risking everything might lose everything they've built with a single careless step because they failed to plan ahead. By beginning with modest goals, they can avoid taking unnecessary risks, progress gradually, and learn throughout the journey.

Maintaining low-risk objectives helps prevent losing what was difficult to obtain or accomplish. Understanding this principle is what enables people to advance in life without allowing their efforts to collapse. It involves taking time to reflect and evaluate what remains to be improved, then working on those areas step by step. Some may say that challenging oneself occasionally is beneficial, but this should be done without risking what has already been built. What good is working so hard only to lose everything due to one thoughtless action? Taking things methodically protects against such outcomes.

In my view, individuals should think carefully before acting, as this is what leads to success rather than allowing everything to fall apart around them. Believing that taking risks without consideration will lead to achievement is misguided. And if one does decide to challenge themselves, they should first contemplate their approach before proceeding.

Should students enter college or the workforce early rather than completing four years of high school? I believe this can be beneficial for many young people.

Some educational institutions provide opportunities for students to prepare for their future goals and pursue them sooner. While some people believe that all students should complete a traditional four-year high school program, I disagree because there are better pathways available for those who are ready to advance.

There are several reasons why early entry can be advantageous. First, starting college earlier allows students to explore their chosen career fields and gain a better understanding of what they want to pursue. They can develop relevant skills and knowledge at a younger age, which helps them become professionals more quickly.

Second, entering the workforce or college early gives students the chance to secure better employment opportunities. They can avoid being stuck in low-income jobs, such as working in restaurants or similar positions, and instead build toward a more promising career.

Third, achieving success at a younger age brings pride to families. Parents appreciate seeing their children on the right path toward a successful future.

In conclusion, completing high school in three years instead of four can make life easier for motivated students. They have the opportunity to learn more, gain valuable experience, and achieve success in a shorter time frame. This approach allows dedicated students to demonstrate their abilities and intelligence earlier in life.

You could be wrong on some of the things that you may see because it maight not be how and what we see, and you could have miss. In 10th grade I miss judged one of my friend because I thought he wasn't the person I wanna talk to. Even tho I had some classes with him I would not talk or be around him, because my impression was that he does not shows respect not only to other students but teachers too , therefor I won't talk to him so he would never know me and won't be mean to me.

However, Later I realize that he was one of my best friend and the nicest person I had ever met, who I can trust and hang out with. Even tho, you may think that you can not change your first impression if you think about it, it might change your first impression.

First impressions can definitely be changed, because things are not always what they seem at first glance. Many people form quick opinions about something or someone without really knowing the truth behind it. We often judge things negatively simply based on what enters our mind when we first see them.

We should avoid making judgments based solely on our initial impressions, as we could easily be mistaken. When we jump to conclusions, we risk misunderstanding people or situations and missing out on something valuable. Different people can have completely different first impressions about the same person without even knowing anything about them. Our initial perception might be incorrect because what we see does not always reflect the full reality.

I experienced this myself in the tenth grade. I misjudged one of my classmates because I thought he was not someone I wanted to associate with. Even though we had several classes together, I refused to talk to him or spend time around him. My impression was that he showed disrespect to both other students and teachers, so I decided to avoid him to protect myself from any rudeness.

However, as time went on, I discovered that he was actually one of the nicest people I have ever met. He became one of my best friends, and I learned that I could completely trust him. This experience taught me that even when we believe our first impression is correct, taking the time to think more deeply about it can lead us to see things differently. Our initial judgments can change when we allow ourselves to look beyond what we first observed.

Dear council members,

I believe the city council should implement a curfew for teenagers because it will help keep them away from trouble. There are some young people who stay out late and cause problems for others in the community. It would be beneficial for teenagers to return home by 10 PM because when they remain on the streets with nothing productive to do, they often engage in behavior that affects others negatively. Additionally, there are other teenagers who are studying for school or trying to get proper rest because they have early morning classes. If the curfew is adopted, there should be a law stating that teenagers who are found on the streets after 10 PM would be breaking the regulations.

Many young people end up in correctional facilities because they become involved in activities they should not participate in. Some of them have access to weapons, but not all of them do. Some teenagers are incarcerated for minor reasons, yet they get grouped together with those who have committed more serious offenses. Not all young people who face legal problems come from difficult circumstances. Some of the issues that teens encounter involve situations created by other individuals in their environment. The city council's proposed curfew is intended to help teenagers avoid these dangerous situations.

Some individuals argue that a curfew interferes with young people's freedom. However, if we consider the alternative perspective, teenagers who are out late often become involved in inappropriate activities. The curfew is simply attempting to guide them toward better choices.

In conclusion, I believe it is a good idea for teenagers to not be on the streets after 10 PM because this will help keep them out of trouble and away from situations that could negatively impact their futures.

Consistency is essential for success in anything we do. Thomas Jefferson, one of America's presidents, understood this principle well and shared it to help people improve their work habits.

When we do something repeatedly, we become better at it. The more we practice, the easier it becomes to perform our tasks effectively. Although repetition can sometimes feel monotonous, it is precisely this regular practice that allows us to master our skills and develop expertise.

I consistently engage in my responsibilities, whether at work, in my studies, or in sports. This routine helps me retain information and deepen my understanding. Through constant practice, we can eventually teach others what we have learned. For instance, reading regularly expands our knowledge about various subjects and different types of people. Those who avoid regular work and neglect their responsibilities tend to remain lazy and fail to acquire new skills.

When we compare diligent individuals with those who lack consistency, the difference becomes evident. Students who complete their homework consistently perform better academically. Those who maintain regular sleep schedules and exercise routines generally enjoy healthier lives. Similarly, people who go to work reliably advance in their careers.

We should encourage others to develop consistent habits and support them in establishing productive routines. When I first started school, I struggled because I did not complete my assignments or study regularly. My friends intervened and taught me the value of consistent effort. I am grateful for this lesson, and I now wish for everyone to understand the importance of regular work.

Additionally, maintaining healthy eating habits consistently keeps us in good physical condition and reduces the need for frequent medical visits.

In conclusion, we should never abandon our routines. Consistency is the key to learning, success, and a healthier life.

Ralph Waldo Emerson once stated, "Unless you try to do something beyond what you have mastered, you will never grow." I completely agree with this statement. To truly grasp what the author means, we must recognize that mastering a skill means being able to perform it perfectly every time. Growth only happens when we step beyond our current abilities and challenge ourselves further.

To genuinely develop as a person, we need to establish objectives for ourselves. Even if the steps we take are modest, they still move us toward achieving something more significant. Mastering any skill requires patience and dedication—it may take years to become proficient at something new. However, with sufficient self-belief and determination, we can eventually reach a level of mastery.

Consider practical examples of this principle in action. If you can ride a bicycle, you could progress to riding a motorcycle. If you know how to make a simple cupcake, you could advance to baking an entire cake. If you have learned to float in water, you could teach yourself to swim properly. These smaller achievements can help us enhance the abilities we already possess. By building on our current skills, we can reach higher levels and accomplish greater feats.

Until we push ourselves beyond our comfort zones, we will never achieve the goals we have set. With the right amount of commitment, we can reach our objectives and expand beyond what we currently know. Just because we cannot accomplish a particular task immediately does not mean we will never master it. We must continue practicing until we become skilled at it. Otherwise, we will never experience personal growth.

In conclusion, the choice is ours to make. We can decide whether we want to develop as individuals or remain unchanged. We can choose to grow and accomplish our life goals, or we can stay the same and never reach our full potential.

I believe that when individuals form their initial impression about something, they have the ability to transform themselves. However, people respond to these impressions in various ways, and nobody possesses identical attitudes.

Some individuals refuse to change because they simply do not care about what others think. Others modify their behavior based on the experiences they have already accumulated throughout their lives. When someone receives a negative impression about themselves, they often begin to reflect on their actions and analyze what went wrong. This process can lead to meaningful transformation, although it requires considerable time and effort.

In relationships, impressions play a significant role. Couples frequently face challenges such as jealousy, toxicity, and harmful influences. Many young people experience emotional pain when they discover their partner has been unfaithful. The betrayal creates a powerful impression that can be difficult to overcome. However, changing one's approach to relationships can ultimately lead to healthier connections with others.

From my own experience, when I first received criticism about my behavior, I believed changing myself was impossible. I was told that I disappointed others with my attitude, and this made me feel extremely negative about myself. I thought I could never excel at things that others did easily. I had become accustomed to behaviors that suited me but troubled those around me. Eventually, I made a decision to transform myself, recognizing that it would be challenging but ultimately achievable with determination and support.

I believe that first impressions can motivate people to change. This transformation demonstrates to others that we are not the same individuals we once were. Each impression we receive offers an opportunity to learn and avoid repeating past mistakes. While forgetting our history entirely may be impossible, daily effort toward improvement leads to meaningful progress. Nobody is perfect, but we can all work toward becoming better by adjusting our attitudes and learning to trust the right people.

I disagree with the idea that principals should force all students to clean up litter or perform community service. This is because many young people already have busy schedules and family responsibilities. However, I think elementary school students could participate since they typically have more free time and fewer commitments. Junior high students who are not involved in sports or other activities might also be able to help.

In some schools, principals might decide to require community service only for students who misbehave. This approach could be effective because troublesome students might learn valuable lessons from such activities. For instance, if disruptive students are required to pick up litter regularly, they might eventually change their behavior because they become exhausted from the work.

Additionally, some students, like myself, could volunteer to help on weekends when we are not occupied with schoolwork. This way, those who are willing and available can contribute without being forced.

Ultimately, I believe community service should be optional for most students, but mandatory only for those who cause problems at school. This way, the students who genuinely need to learn discipline can benefit, while others are not burdened with additional obligations.

Being part of a team versus working independently.

Having the opportunity to collaborate with a group of capable and like-minded individuals can certainly be rewarding. However, there are significant advantages to working solo. When you work by yourself, you don't have to worry about others taking credit for your contributions or copying your work, which frequently occurs in group settings.

Team-based work often resembles a situation where individuals contribute less effort. What I mean is that when people work together, they tend to share responsibilities, which can make someone appear dependent on others for support. This creates a sense of insecurity, as if the person cannot accomplish tasks without constant assistance.

Collaborating with others has its drawbacks. As a student, I enjoy working with my friends, but they often imitate my work, which frustrates me. It makes me feel that they wouldn't succeed without my input. It's unfortunate that some people always need to be part of a team to perform well, especially when they aren't the ones actually doing the work.

I prefer working alone rather than in a team. This isn't because I dislike collaborating with others—it's simply my nature. When I work with others, I feel it doesn't benefit me since they either cheat or fail to contribute meaningfully. Working independently allows me to be myself and motivates me to continue without worrying about others. It makes me feel capable of achieving more without needing assistance.

Throughout my life, I've learned important lessons. I've discovered that you must prioritize yourself and look out for your own interests. In my view, relying too much on groups is unnecessary. You should never feel worthless, and you should always consider your own wellbeing first.

A frequently discussed topic nowadays is whether students should be expected to choose a specific career path by the time they start high school. Many educational systems require young people to select their courses based on the profession they wish to pursue in the future. In my opinion, expecting teenagers to commit to a career at such a young age is not a reasonable expectation. Adolescents are simply not mature enough to make such an important life decision.

The first reason why this approach is problematic is that high school students lack the necessary experience to make informed career choices. At this stage in their lives, they have had very limited exposure to the working world. Most teenagers have never held a real job or spent significant time in a professional environment. How can they possibly know what career suits them when they have never actually experienced any type of work? Without this essential experience, students are essentially making blind decisions about their future.

Additionally, teenagers tend to be impulsive and often change their minds about what they want. When students select certain subjects in their freshman year, they may later discover that the field does not interest them as much as they thought. For instance, a student might choose technology classes because they seem appealing, only to realize later that the reality of the profession does not match their expectations. This can lead to wasted time and effort, as they must then start over with different subjects.

Furthermore, young people often lack the maturity to think seriously about long-term consequences. Many teenagers are more focused on immediate concerns rather than planning for their adult lives. They may select courses without fully understanding how these choices will affect their future opportunities.

In conclusion, I believe that students should not be pressured to decide on a career during high school. Instead, they should be encouraged to explore different subjects and gradually develop an understanding of their interests and strengths. By the time they reach their senior year or begin college, they will be better equipped to make a thoughtful and informed decision about their professional future.

I strongly agree with Ralph Waldo Emerson's statement that "Unless you try to do something beyond what you have already mastered, you will never grow." Throughout my seventeen years of life, I have come to understand that remaining in one's comfort zone leads to stagnation. When we become too comfortable, we lose the motivation to push ourselves toward our full potential.

Staying in a state of of ease may feel pleasant, but it ultimately prevents personal development. The time and effort we spend remaining comfortable could be used to become better individuals and to share our knowledge with others. It is essential that we constantly strive to reach our highest capabilities.

I believe most people should embrace this perspective because refusing to improve oneself is not a constructive approach to life. While pushing beyond our limits may sometimes bring challenges and difficulties, the rewards are worthwhile. Expanding our knowledge and abilities allows us to assist those who cannot help themselves. As human beings, we have a responsibility to support one another, even in small ways. Many individuals hesitate to ask for assistance, so we should offer help without waiting to be asked.

However, some people may hold a different view. They might prioritize their own comfort or believe they have already reached a sufficient level of achievement. These individuals may feel they have mastered their problems and situations, thinking there is nothing left to learn. This perspective is incorrect. We can always continue developing as people, whether as parents, children, friends, or professionals. The key is never to settle for mediocrity.

Instead of remaining in our comfort zones, we should focus on daily improvement. Learning something new each day and offering help to others creates positive change. Engaging with other people and gaining knowledge will only benefit us.

Emerson's words represent an undeniable truth. By committing to continuous growth, we can become individuals worthy of admiration and respect. We should all aspire to become better versions of ourselves.

Yes, I believe students would benefit greatly from being able to attend classes from home because they would be more prepared to learn and able to concentrate better.

The main reason I hold this view is that sometimes at school, students feel embarrassed to show their true abilities. Even an intelligent student might tell themselves they cannot do anything or speak English well. However, if someone wants to achieve their goals, they can do it without going to school.

For example, if a student is at home alone with no one telling them what to do or how to do things correctly, but they have many questions about their online class, they will try to find ways to solve the problems by themselves. Additionally, if someone is at home, they can find new information and work throughout the day. When they get hungry, they can quickly go to the kitchen to make something to eat and then return to their room to continue with their homework. If they have a question, they can ask a teacher for help through messaging.

Eventually, attending classes at home without pressure could be different and more comfortable for students who are shy or perhaps need a teacher to explain things only to them individually. For those students who do not like waking up too early in the morning, they have the choice to study later at night without needing to be ready for school. In many cases, when girls become pregnant, they can still attend school, but it is difficult for them to continue studying while pregnant and after giving birth. I know this because a friend told me and other girls about the process she had to go through during her pregnancy and after having her baby. I do not know how hard it was, but I can imagine being in that position. What did my friend do? During her pregnancy, she still came to school. I saw her many times, and she was so tired with her belly. Then, when she had her baby, she took the next classes at her house. I was surprised, and I do not know how uncomfortable it was for her to have a teacher with her when the baby started crying or needed to eat. Later, she went back to school, but she did not feel okay about leaving her baby at home. This story made me think that if I had the choice to choose how to study, I would prefer to take classes at home rather than at school.

I think students would benefit from being able to attend classes from home, which is a great idea. However, there are many problems. What happens if a student does not have money to pay for online classes, or if their families do not have the resources to help them? Another reason is that we have to work and make money for ourselves, so we miss many days at school because we want to sleep more hours, or we come to school but do not pay attention to what the teacher is saying. So, I think if a student needs money and needs to work, they can continue studying online, and maybe in that way, it is easier to pass the class and the SOL. Attending classes at home online helps students in these cases go to work for a few hours and then come home for the rest of the day to study. Another option is working one day and not working the next day while taking online classes. In summary, never give up. When we want something that we cannot get anywhere else, only our effort can make it possible. Also, we should ask for help when we do not understand something and put our best effort into everything, including trying to solve problems, researching good information, and the most important thing we have to do is study. Sometimes other people make us feel bad or like we do not belong in this world. We should go ahead and demonstrate to those people who do not believe in us that we can do it.

During the school year, it is possible to learn through online video conferencing. In the videos, they explain clearly how to solve math exercises or other kinds of materials. Examples of benefits of attending classes at home are spending more time on the computer, focusing more on homework, using the phone for information whenever we want, studying all day, not talking with friends during class, and finishing more quickly with no distractions. All these things are benefits if students attend classes at their home. In winter, they do not have to worry about how cold it is outside in the morning or what clothes are appropriate for school. They do not have to come to school in a good mood to see someone they do not want to see and avoid getting involved in problems with other students. It can be better to stay at home alone in their own class than to go to school. Many students suffer from depression, and that is so bad for them. If schools give them the opportunity to take classes online, it is much better for their health. This is my opinion about attending classes at home.

When I was younger, I would often see this happening. People would drop their things, and I would pick them up and give them back or tell them they had dropped something. Usually, when people find items lying around, the first thing they think about is taking it. However, that is not very smart because you never know whose it is or where it came from. Nobody leaves their stuff somewhere and just walks away without knowing or caring about it. Needing something means you have to have it or it is really important to you. If you do not have it, you would struggle to find a replacement. But if you really need something, you can probably buy it from a nearby store. Wanting something is different. You do not have to have it, but you want it to show off or to have fun with it. You do not really need it, but you just want to take something that you could buy, even though you are not struggling or going through any trouble. You just felt like doing the action and did not really care about the consequences.

I believe that helping others achieve their dreams and goals is one of the most valuable things a person can do in life. My opinion agrees with Emerson's view on this matter, and I support my central idea with three main reasons: making something meaningful for others, having a specific career purpose, and using one's skills to assist people.

First, it is essential to create positive change for other people who need support. When we help others accomplish their dreams, we give them reasons to move forward and pursue their goals. For instance, when someone wants to grow professionally, their family feels proud of their achievements. Additionally, providing encouragement to others allows them to fulfill their purposes in life. This creates a ripple effect of positivity that benefits entire communities.

Second, having a specific job that allows you to help many people is truly rewarding. There are careers designed to assist others in reaching their full potential. In such roles, you can provide valuable information about different professions and the opportunities available in each field. You can also help people discover what they truly want to achieve and guide them toward excellent career paths. For example, helping someone find information about their ideal career can lead to amazing results in their life. The satisfaction of seeing others succeed because of your guidance is immense.

Third, possessing a skill that enables you to support others represents a great accomplishment. When you decide to help people who are eager to progress and achieve their goals, you are using your abilities for a meaningful purpose. If you have strong abilities to assist others in reaching success, this can be incredibly rewarding both for them and for you. These skills become even more valuable when shared with those who need them.

In conclusion, supporting others in finding their greatest accomplishments and purposes in life brings lasting happiness. When we help people achieve their dreams, we experience fulfillment in our own lives as well. We should never stop pursuing our own goals while also helping others reach theirs. The key is to keep moving forward and continue dreaming big while assisting others to do the same.

Modifying the school cafeteria menu is not a wise decision because many students may refuse to eat the new options, some pupils could have allergic reactions, and the institution might waste money on food that simply gets thrown away.

At this age, young people tend to be extremely particular about what they eat. Students often inspect their meals carefully before deciding whether to consume them. If the food appears unappealing or has an unusual smell, most students will either discard it completely or simply go hungry until they return home. As someone who considers myself quite selective about food, I can understand this behavior well—if I am going to eat something, I really want it to look appetizing and fresh.

Educational institutions should maintain their current lunch menus because they may not be aware of every student's dietary restrictions. Many children have allergies or food sensitivities that are not commonly discussed. Unfortunately, some students feel embarrassed about having such conditions and hesitate to disclose them to school staff due to fear of being ridiculed by their peers. Therefore, making changes to the menu without proper knowledge of these issues could potentially put students at risk.

Many schools have sufficient budgets to provide various services for their students. Administrators might believe that introducing new menu items will increase student satisfaction. However, they often overlook the fact that numerous children are extremely particular about their food choices. When students reject the new offerings and discard them, the school suffers financially. This situation is counterproductive because the resources spent on menu modifications could be utilized more effectively elsewhere.

Educational institutions should simply preserve their existing lunch menus rather than attempting to change them. The intended benefits do not materialize because students refuse to eat the modified dishes, resulting in significant waste. Additionally, the lack of information about student allergies creates potential health hazards. By keeping the current menus unchanged, schools can avoid these problems entirely. They will conserve financial resources, students will continue to enjoy familiar meals, and no pupil will experience any adverse reactions.

Have you ever wondered why people graduate at such a young age? Is it because they are smarter than their classmates?

Although some might argue that graduating in three years is a bad idea, actually graduating in three years is a good idea because you are more mature for the real world and you are able to take full responsibility for your own actions.

The first reason why graduating in three years is a good idea is that you will be more mature for the real world. Many people today do not know how the real world works. For example, many teenagers do not know how the real world works; they drink and drive, get involved in accidents, and hurt themselves and other people without thinking about their actions because their parents bail them out of problems, so they don't care if they hurt someone or not. All they know is that someone will take care of them. This shows that if teenagers graduate in three years, they will be more mature for the real world and they will learn what to do and not what to do.

Another example is that parents take teenage children for granted; for example, they pay for car insurance. If teenagers break the law, parents stand up for them and say "my child is innocent." Because parents defend them if they do something wrong, they convince themselves they are doing the right thing. By the time it is too late for them, they think that is how the real world works, and they won't be able to learn from their mistakes. This shows that teenagers graduating in three years will help them to know their surroundings, know the full consequences of their actions, and take full responsibility for their own behavior.

The second reason why it is a good idea for teenagers to graduate early is that they will take full responsibility of their own. They will pay house rent and bills, light bills, for example. My mom pays for the phone bill so I don't really care where the money comes from; all I know is that someone pays the bill. This shows that teenagers will be more responsible if they pay their own bills and care about bills not going up. Another example is I used to use too much light and water, so when the water and light bills come, they go up; my mom is the only one who has to pay the bills. This shows that if teenagers don't know how much they use, it's because others take care of those things for them.

However, some might argue that graduating in three years is a bad idea because you miss out on life. You don't know how to have fun; you will be stressed out and you won't know what makes you happy. Another example is that you should enjoy the moments you have as a teenager.

Thomas Jefferson once wrote "it is wonderful how much may be done if we are doing." This statement suggests that when we constantly keep ourselves occupied with tasks, whether for our personal benefit or for society, we can achieve remarkable results. The question is: do we truly accomplish more by always staying active, or does inactivity also have its value? Some people argue that rest is essential because it allows us to recharge and return to work with renewed energy. However, others believe that continuous action is superior because hard work leads to achieving our goals and contributing meaningfully to society.

Every day, millions of people wake up early and dedicate themselves to their work, giving their best effort. But what about those who are unable to find employment? Even in such situations, individuals can still contribute to society or focus on their personal development. They can volunteer, help others, or engage in activities that promote growth. Being an active member of the community is what truly matters.

It is important to acknowledge that everyone needs some time to rest. Nevertheless, excessive relaxation can prevent us from reaching our dreams and accomplishing our objectives. Consistently engaging in positive activities is beneficial when we approach them with dedication and passion. Every working individual has a reason for their efforts. Some people are striving to achieve specific goals, while others simply enjoy their work and need to provide for their families. My mother always tells me that if I want something, I should pursue it actively. We all desire a better future, which is why staying productive is essential.

From a societal perspective, people must remain active regardless of their personal circumstances. We have bills to pay, taxes to cover, and basic needs to meet, which requires us to have some form of work. Beyond employment, there are many other ways to stay productive, such as helping others. These activities contribute to our personal growth and development. Whether we receive payment or not, when we genuinely care about making a positive difference in the world, we will naturally engage in meaningful work.

Taking action is vital for humanity because it allows our world to progress and develop. Our dreams and ambitions drive us to pursue our daily activities. Consider whether being productive or remaining inactive has a greater impact on shaping our minds and futures. In conclusion, Jefferson's quote encourages us to reflect on what we are doing and what we should be doing with our lives. While taking occasional breaks is beneficial, we must never forget that we have dreams and goals that we need to transform into reality.

In my opinion, self-esteem develops through achievement. When students put in effort and earn recognition, they feel proud of themselves and gradually build genuine confidence. The connection between working hard and receiving rewards is clear, and this process is essential for developing healthy self-esteem.

Many students work diligently, submit their assignments on time, and even hold part-time jobs after school. However, some of these students struggle to develop true self-esteem because they lack self-confidence. The truth is, you cannot build self-esteem without first believing in yourself. Confidence is the foundation upon which self-esteem is constructed.

On the other hand, there are students who feel confident but do not achieve anything meaningful. They may have a positive attitude, but without working toward goals, they cannot develop real self-esteem. This shows that both confidence and achievement are necessary.

Students should strive to earn achievements because these accomplishments encourage them and help them build self-esteem. They can develop self-esteem by working hard, being punctual, and organizing their tasks using a planner or calendar. Having a clear plan helps students stay focused and track their progress.

Unfortunately, many students today do not work hard enough. I am not sure whether technology has made them lazy or whether they simply lack motivation. Regardless, they are not trying to achieve their goals at school. It frustrates me to see this because if these students would simply study for a couple of hours at home, they could earn many achievements and reach their potential.

To build true self-esteem, students need to earn achievements and become confident first. Only then can they become the best version of themselves.

Teachers also play an important role in this process. Students often spend more time with their teachers than with their parents during the week. I do not expect teachers to have long conversations with every student about self-esteem unless the student is proactive and asks for guidance. However, teachers can at least show students the right path to achieve their goals. This is enough to make students think about their achievements and start working on their confidence and self-esteem.

I can speak from personal experience. When I moved to the United States in 2017, I did not speak English and had no friends at school. It was extremely difficult to attend school without being able to communicate with anyone. I was also very shy. Whenever someone tried to talk to me, my face would turn red because I lacked confidence.

I decided to work hard to learn the language and make friends. Now, I can speak, read, and write English well. I have become much more confident, made many friends, and actually enjoy going to school.

In conclusion, self-confidence and working hard for achievements are the keys to building self-esteem. Students should focus on their studies and earn achievements, which will help them develop self-esteem. They should also be encouraged by their parents and believe in themselves.

I agree with Emerson's statement because when you master a skill, you perform better at your job, you receive better opportunities, and you achieve higher positions than those without expertise.

However, not everyone shares this view. Some people believe that individuals without formal mastery can sometimes perform better than those who have it.

First, when you have mastered a skill, you work more effectively in your field. This is because you have spent years studying and practicing. For instance, in a restaurant, a person who has mastered culinary arts only needs to remember recipes, while someone without that mastery must also learn about ingredients, equipment, and cooking techniques.

Second, having a mastery qualification opens doors to better opportunities. Your degree or certificate demonstrates that you are prepared for the job. Many companies require specific qualifications for certain positions. For example, some restaurants will only hire someone as a manager if they have a hospitality degree, and these positions also come with higher salaries.

Third, you can obtain better positions than those without mastery because your experience is recognized. For example, if a restaurant needs staff for the kitchen, management, and dishwashing, someone with a culinary degree is more likely to be hired as a manager. Meanwhile, an unqualified applicant will probably start as a dishwasher and would need much more time and effort to advance.

In conclusion, individuals with mastery qualifications have better job opportunities, perform more effectively in their work, and achieve higher positions than those without them. For this reason, I agree with Emerson's statement that without mastery, you cannot truly grow.

The Four-Day School Week

There has been considerable discussion recently about whether schools should shift from the traditional five-day week to a four-day schedule. After carefully examining both sides of this debate, I strongly believe that implementing a four-day school week would be highly beneficial for students, teachers, and families alike.

One of the main concerns about reducing school days is how to make up for the lost instructional time. However, this problem can be solved by extending each school day by approximately two hours. This adjustment would actually provide students with more concentrated learning time, allowing them to focus better on their lessons and complete classroom projects without feeling rushed. Additionally, students would have greater opportunities to seek support from their teachers when they are struggling with particular subjects.

The extra day off would offer numerous valuable possibilities for students. Those who enjoy reading could spend more time in the library, while students interested in athletics could use the day for additional practice. Furthermore, the fifth day could be reserved for medical appointments and other health-related matters, which would significantly reduce the number of absences during regular school hours. Currently, many students miss important lessons because their parents cannot schedule doctor visits outside of school time.

Teachers would also benefit considerably from this arrangement. Many educators are parents themselves and would appreciate having an extra day to spend with their families and handle personal responsibilities. This would likely improve teacher morale and job satisfaction, ultimately benefiting their students as well.

Different student groups would find particular advantages in this system. Seniors facing important decisions about their future would have more time to research universities, explore scholarship options, and prepare for higher education. Freshmen transitioning from middle school would benefit from having additional time to adjust to their new environment and participate in extracurricular activities without feeling overwhelmed.

The free day could also be utilized for community service activities. With proper parental permission and adult supervision, students could participate in neighborhood cleanup efforts or other volunteer work. Schools might even establish programs connecting students with local businesses offering part-time employment opportunities on these days.

Of course, some concerns exist regarding this proposal. Students who work part-time jobs might initially find their available working hours reduced. Nevertheless, they could use their free day for full-time work or pick up additional weekend shifts. While attending school and working simultaneously can be exhausting, the extended weekend would provide students with more time to rest, complete homework, and maintain a healthier balance between their responsibilities.

When weighing the advantages against the disadvantages, it becomes clear that the benefits substantially outweigh the drawbacks for the majority of students. While every individual's circumstances differ, the four-day week would provide flexibility for various needs, whether that involves family time, household responsibilities, employment, or additional study.

In conclusion, I firmly believe that implementing a four-day school week would represent a positive change for high school and college students. By working together to advocate for this modification, we could create a more balanced and effective educational system that better serves the needs of today's students.

Many people argue about whether students should be required to take elective classes in school or if they should be allowed to choose freely. I believe that students should have the freedom to select their own electives because this helps them discover their talents, stay motivated, and prepare for a successful future.

When students are forced to take classes they are not interested in, they often feel bored and unmotivated. This leads to skipping classes, which results in poor grades. When students receive bad grades, they become frustrated and lose interest in learning altogether. Without passing their classes, they may not earn enough credits to graduate. Failing to complete high school means they cannot attend college or university, and finding a good job becomes extremely difficult. In fact, some people without jobs may even face homelessness. This is why it is so important for students to choose subjects that genuinely interest them.

Every person has unique abilities and talents. Students should have the opportunity to explore these strengths by taking electives in areas where they excel. When a student is good at something, they naturally enjoy participating in that class. This enjoyment leads to better grades and a genuine desire to learn more. Additionally, students who develop strong skills in their chosen electives can benefit greatly in the future. Companies are often looking for talented individuals, and having specialized abilities can open many doors. For instance, a student who is talented in drama could potentially be hired by a production company, become an actor, star in films, and earn a substantial income. Furthermore, students are not limited to developing just one skill. They can acquire multiple abilities, which will only increase their chances of success in life. Having various experiences and knowledge is extremely valuable in today's competitive world.

Looking ahead to the future is essential for every student. When young people take electives that they love and are passionate about, they can use these skills to build a successful career after graduating from high school and college. Adulthood brings many challenges, but having developed strong skills through elective classes helps students overcome difficulties more easily. These skills also allow students to pursue their dreams and create the future they desire. With proper preparation, students will know exactly what direction they want to take in life and can work confidently toward their goals. Many students will discover their true calling and purpose through these elective courses.

Of course, some people argue that requiring electives might not be effective because students may lack motivation or may not take the classes seriously. However, I believe that when students are given the freedom to choose subjects they genuinely care about, they are much more likely to stay engaged and committed to their studies.

Should Students Design Their Own Summer Projects?

In my view, students should be allowed to create their own projects during summer vacation rather than having assignments designed by teachers. There are several reasons why this approach would be more beneficial for learners.

The first reason is that students are aware of their own strengths and weaknesses. Each student knows which subjects or skills they find difficult and need to improve. When they are given the freedom to choose their own projects, they can focus on areas where they need more practice. For instance, as an ESL learner, I prefer to work on personal projects during summer so that I do not forget what I have learned throughout the school year.

The second reason is that students feel more comfortable and confident when working on projects they have chosen themselves. When students create their own work, they fully understand the topic because they have selected it based on their interests. This makes the project easier to complete and more engaging. In contrast, assignments given by teachers may not match what students need or care about.

Additionally, creating personal projects helps students retain what they have learned. If students stop practicing during the summer break, they risk forgetting important material. By continuing to work on their own projects, they stay active and maintain their knowledge. This is especially important for language learners who need consistent practice to avoid losing progress.

Finally, allowing students to design their own projects enables them to demonstrate their abilities independently. When students work without constant teacher guidance, they become more self-reliant and creative. They have the opportunity to explore their interests and develop new skills at their own pace.

In conclusion, I strongly believe that students should design their own summer projects. This method helps them address their individual needs, remember what they have learned, and develop confidence in their abilities.

Ralph Waldo Emerson once stated that being yourself in a world that constantly tries to change you is the greatest achievement. In today's society, our actions, accomplishments, and behavior define who we are. Many people around the world believe that going beyond what is expected shows humility and a generous spirit. For instance, at work, in school, or in our community, doing things that are not really our responsibility demonstrates a kind heart and a willingness to make a positive difference. I agree with this idea because when we stay true to ourselves, others recognize something special in us. They want to learn from us, and even if we do not succeed perfectly at first, we should never give up trying to stand out. For example, at school, you might help a classmate understand a math problem even though it is the teacher's job to explain. Your kind action inspires others to do the same, and soon more people will behave in this generous way.

Second, being yourself is important because you become an inspiration to those around you. This can happen in many places, such as at home, in your neighborhood, at school, or even at church. If your neighbors see you keeping your yard clean or helping others with tasks like cutting grass, they may feel motivated to do the same. Your genuine character can encourage others to be better.

Finally, being yourself is significant because your accomplishments can change how others think. When people see your progress and success, they ask themselves how you managed to achieve it. You can share your story and show them that if you could do it, they can too. For example, in a family where some members have low-paying jobs while others run their own businesses, a helpful and positive person can spread good vibes, hope, and motivation to everyone.

Establishing a homework club is an excellent approach to enhancing student performance. In my view, such a program offers numerous benefits, including better academic results, increased leisure time, reduced stress, and the opportunity to receive assistance from both teachers and peers.

First and foremost, a homework club provides valuable academic support that can lead to improved grades. When students work together with educators and classmates, they accomplish more tasks effectively. They also have additional study opportunities and feel more confident about upcoming tests. For instance, if a student struggles with a particular problem, they can stay after classes and receive the guidance they need to understand the material better.

Additionally, students who participate in homework clubs actually enjoy more free time once they return home. With their work completed at school, they can dedicate their evening hours to family, friends, and recreational activities. I would personally welcome such an opportunity because after a long school day, most students prefer to relax or socialize rather than struggle with difficult assignments. Furthermore, knowing that others face similar challenges creates a supportive environment where everyone can assist one another.

Moreover, homework clubs help students feel less exhausted. When learners receive help with their studies, they experience less anxiety about their academic performance. This means they can rest properly and wake up feeling refreshed for the next school day. Given the various pressures young people face today, schools should strive to make their lives easier rather than more demanding.

Finally, students should appreciate having access to such resources. Many young people put forth great effort but become discouraged when they encounter difficulties. A homework club reminds them that success is achievable and that support is available whenever they need it.

In conclusion, implementing a homework club greatly benefits students by helping them achieve better academic results, allowing them more free time at home, reducing their fatigue, and showing them that help is always within reach.

One of my greatest strengths is my ability to create visual art, particularly through drawing. When I work on pieces, I gravitate toward subjects like starry skies, moonlit scenes, forests, and oceans. Drawing is a remarkable skill that allows individuals to express themselves through various artistic forms. There are numerous styles to explore, but my personal favorite is freehand drawing because it gives me complete creative freedom. Unlike some other art forms, drawing permits me to correct errors and refine my work until it meets my vision.

Painting is another medium I deeply enjoy, as it enables me to convey my emotions directly onto the canvas. Whether I'm feeling joyful, melancholy, frustrated, or excited, I can translate those feelings into color and form. Art represents one of my greatest passions because it allows me to bring my imagination to life. Interestingly, many people are willing to pay substantial sums for original artwork, sometimes even billions of dollars, simply because they find it beautiful and meaningful.

Many individuals possess artistic talent, though some are so self-critical that they discard their work, believing it lacks value. What they often fail to recognize is that others might genuinely appreciate and even pay for their creations. While valuable art pieces are sometimes sold for enormous prices, other artists choose to keep their work for personal reasons, such as preserving memories or sharing it with family. Occasionally, they sell pieces to loved ones at modest prices because the transaction is about sentiment rather than profit.

Some collectors have acquired artwork that artists themselves considered flawed but chose not to discard. These pieces sometimes become valuable precisely because of their unique imperfections.

I believe artists should consider selling their work because it can generate significant income. However, creating art requires considerable patience, as mistakes may necessitate starting over. Rather than beginning anew, skilled artists often transform errors into beautiful elements, demonstrating how art can turn something seemingly ugly into something aesthetically pleasing.

Skeptics might claim that art is dull, but this perspective changes when one genuinely loves the process. When I'm enthusiastic about creating, I lose track of perfectionism and allow my instincts to guide my hand. The result is liberating and exhilarating.

Frustration can arise when the final product doesn't match one's vision, and I certainly experience this disappointment. Nevertheless, patience remains essential because art demands dedication. With practice, challenges become more manageable. I'm continually developing my skills, and while difficulties persist, I understand that consistent practice leads to improvement.

Do students really gain anything from being able to attend classes remotely? In my opinion, they do not. I once knew someone who participated in online schooling from home, and she never completed her assignments. She used this opportunity to focus on other matters instead, and she gained nothing from the experience. Students do not benefit from remote learning because they abuse the freedom it provides, fail to complete their responsibilities, and essentially learn nothing.

To begin with, students misuse the ability to attend classes from home by using that time for personal activities. For instance, they submit assignments long after the deadline has passed. While not every student who studies from home takes advantage of this situation, those who do simply want to enjoy themselves rather than focus on their schoolwork. They also frequently invent various reasons why they could not finish their tasks. They utilize their free time to go out with friends, attend social gatherings, spend time with romantic partners, and engage in other activities unrelated to their education.

Furthermore, students simply do not complete the work they are expected to do. When they receive homework or projects, they behave carelessly and neglect to do them because they know there is no one watching over them, such as a teacher reminding them to stay on task. They spend most of their time on other activities instead of finishing their assignments. They prioritize going to parties and hanging out with friends over completing work that would actually benefit them in the future. Many students already understand the material but simply choose not to complete any tasks because they lack the motivation.

Ultimately, students learn absolutely nothing by attending classes from home. All they do is go to parties, spend time with friends, and be with their partners. They do not complete the work assigned to them. Instead, they either copy answers from other people or find solutions online. Most students view remote learning as a chance to have fun and take a break from traditional schooling. They learn nothing because they spend their time playing around when they should be taking their studies seriously. They merely want to enjoy themselves all day without worrying about their schoolwork.

In conclusion, students do not benefit from being able to attend classes from home because they exploit this option to focus on other matters, they fail to do what is required of them, and they gain no actual knowledge. All they do is go to parties, spend time with friends, and be with their partners. They do not complete any of the tasks that have been assigned to them.

When creating something original, there is no need to seek suggestions from others or copy from the internet. Relying on one's own thinking builds genuine confidence.

Furthermore, following one's instincts is important because it enables individuals to handle problems independently. When challenges arise, people should not have to wait for others to solve them. Having confidence in oneself means being able to face difficulties without constantly seeking guidance from others.

Additionally, believing in oneself affects how others perceive us. For instance, when giving a presentation in class, if a student does not believe they can do well, the teacher may also doubt their abilities. This lack of self-confidence can negatively impact grades because the student will constantly seek reassurance from the teacher about whether they are doing things correctly.

In conclusion, I strongly feel that people should make their own decisions and trust their own judgment before asking for help. Self-belief is crucial because if individuals do not have confidence in themselves, others will not believe in them either. Ultimately, everyone should value their own opinions and instincts, rather than simply following what others say. Listening to oneself is the foundation of true self-worth.

Many schools create programs that bring together older and younger students, and these initiatives can be very beneficial for everyone involved. These programs allow both groups to learn from each other and develop important skills.

Older students can share their experiences and knowledge with younger students. They can teach them about the mistakes they made in the past so that the younger students can avoid making the same errors. This way, younger students learn what is right and wrong without having to discover everything by themselves. Older students also have more experience with responsibilities, so they can help younger students understand what to expect as they grow older.

Younger students also benefit from these programs in many ways. They can receive support when they face problems or have questions. In some schools, younger students may not speak English well, and older students can help them with this. Additionally, younger students can learn from the mistakes that older students share, which helps them make better decisions in their own lives.

The relationship works in both directions. Sometimes older students need help too. They can ask younger students for assistance with certain tasks or subjects. This creates a mutual exchange where everyone supports each other. When conflicts arise between younger students, older students can step in to help resolve the situation and guide them toward the right path.

However, there are some challenges with these programs. Occasionally, older students may not want to help, and younger students may not want to listen to their advice. This can be similar to how some teenagers do not want to follow what adults or teachers tell them. When people ignore warnings, they often face negative consequences later.

Despite these difficulties, these programs are valuable because they teach students how to work together and support one another. Older students act like mentors who can guide younger students through life challenges. In return, younger students bring fresh perspectives and energy to the relationship. Together, they can create a positive learning environment where everyone grows and develops. The key is that both groups need each other, and when they cooperate, they can achieve great things.
