Accelerating graduation by taking summer courses is not the best approach for most students. I hold this view because learners may require additional credits to complete their diploma, many rely on summer employment for income, and some simply need time away from academics to recharge.

My first concern involves credit requirements. Students who attempt to finish in three years often discover they lack sufficient credits to graduate. When this happens, they must overload their schedule with extra classes, which creates unnecessary pressure and anxiety. A traditional four-year pathway allows students to participate in extracurricular activities such as clubs and sports while maintaining a manageable course load. These activities strengthen college applications and help young people develop important skills. Trying to balance an excessive number of classes with other commitments can quickly become overwhelming.

Secondly, many students depend on summer work to earn money. Teenagers need financial resources for various purposes, including saving for a vehicle or future college expenses. Summer vacation provides the ideal opportunity to work full-time without the distraction of homework and tests. If students were required to attend classes during this period, they would have less time available for employment. This loss of income could prevent them from reaching their financial goals or force them to work during the school year, which might negatively impact their academic performance.

Finally, students deserve a break after months of intensive study. Some young people use their final year to reflect on their career aspirations or simply to rest before beginning the next chapter of their lives. Taking time off allows them to work full-time and accumulate savings for future needs like tuition or living expenses. Rushing through education without adequate rest can lead to burnout and exhaustion. Success in life requires patience and steady progress rather than attempting to accomplish everything as quickly as possible.

In summary, graduating in three years rather than four presents significant challenges. Students may find themselves short on required credits, lose valuable time for summer employment, and miss the opportunity for a much-needed break. These factors make accelerated graduation an impractical choice for most learners.

Many people wonder whether we actually decide who we become or whether external factors shape us. The famous British naturalist and politician John Lubbock once said, "Your character will be what you yourself choose to make it." I completely agree with this statement because I believe we have the power to select our own character traits, such as being reserved, outgoing, or confident. These personal qualities are decisions we make, which is why I support Lubbock's viewpoint.

To begin with, I think we choose whether to be quiet or reserved. Being quiet is not inherently positive or negative; it simply depends on the situation. Sometimes silence is appropriate, while other times we need to speak up. Looking back at my own experience, I was quite shy during my middle school years, specifically in sixth and seventh grade. I rarely spoke to anyone and had very few friends. This loneliness motivated me to change, so I started engaging with others more often. As a result, I made many new friends and felt much happier. This demonstrates that we can control our personality traits and choose to modify them when necessary.

Another trait we can select is being sociable. Being outgoing offers numerous benefits, including making friends, gaining new knowledge, and discovering different perspectives. During seventh and eighth grade, I became a very talkative person. I learned valuable skills like how to approach strangers and hold conversations. I also discovered interesting things about human nature, such as the fact that people can change over time. Some individuals start out kind but become moody, while others who were once unkind eventually become nicer. Of course, some people never change, and that is simply part of life. This experience reinforced my belief that we can choose to be social and develop this characteristic.

Finally, we can also choose to be confident or self-assured. Having confidence is generally a positive quality, though it can become negative if we become arrogant or overconfident. Some people dislike those who are too full of themselves, considering them unpleasant to be around. I must admit that I was somewhat cocky and overly confident when I was younger, particularly in sports. I was extremely competitive and would often shout with joy when I scored or won a game. While some might argue that our character traits are influenced by factors beyond our control, I see it differently. When I yelled excitedly, I could have chosen to celebrate more quietly, perhaps by simply raising my hands or looking up at the sky. The fact that I had this choice proves we can control our traits.

In conclusion, John Lubbock's statement that we choose our own character is accurate. We decide whether to be quiet, outgoing, or confident based on our experiences and the choices we make. Our character is not simply handed to us; it is something we actively create through our daily decisions.

Many people view failure as something negative that should be avoided at all costs. In our everyday lives, we often try to stay away from situations where we might fail. Only a small number of individuals are willing to face their fears and embrace failure as a valuable learning experience. These brave people understand that failure can lead to great achievements.

Fear influences many aspects of our lives. We worry about how others perceive us and whether we have made the right choices. Most importantly, we fear failure because we are uncertain about the outcome of our actions. This concern divides people into two different groups: those who play it safe and those who are willing to take risks. Both approaches have advantages and disadvantages.

People who choose the safe path rely on their existing knowledge and experience. They prefer to stay within their comfort zones and avoid situations where they might fail. The word "shy" does not fully describe them, except when they encounter something new and unfamiliar. They simply refuse to take risks, which means they will never fail—but they will also never succeed. This can apply to various situations, such as answering a question in class, trying a new sport, going to the gym, or wearing different clothes. The only thing holding them back is fear. They never discover what might have happened if they had tried. When they do attempt something and fail, they see it as a defeat. One possible benefit of their mindset is that they avoid losses, but they also miss out on opportunities for success. These individuals often have previous negative experiences that make them afraid to try again. Perhaps they once said something embarrassing in class and everyone laughed, or they tried a sport but were not good at it, or they felt uncomfortable at the gym because they were not as strong as others.

On the other hand, people who actively try new things and gain experience are often the ones who achieve meaningful results in their lives. A great example is Winston Churchill, the former British Prime Minister. His life demonstrates the importance of perseverance. If we consider how he became Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, we can see that his path was not easy. His biography reveals how many times he attempted things and failed, yet he ultimately achieved success. People like Churchill view failures as valuable life lessons. For them, failure is part of the process of perfecting an idea, succeeding in an action, making the right decision, or giving the correct answer. When they fail, they face the consequences and, more importantly, they feel proud—not of failing, but of the correction and the knowledge they have gained. This knowledge drives them to avoid similar mistakes in the future. They may make the same mistake again, but in the end, they become winners. This is where enthusiasm becomes essential.

People work toward their goals, and enthusiasm motivates them to continue. Winston Churchill won World War II because his goal was not to fail his people and everything he had built. Enthusiasm can take many forms, such as duty for a president, joy for a musician, or happiness for a parent. Maintaining enthusiasm depends on the individual. The size of the goal does not matter—what matters is the person's commitment. Anyone can become president if they truly want it, but some people cannot even go to the gym a few times a week because they are lazy and lack determination. This connects closely with our life goals, whether short-term or long-term. Enthusiasm can be weakened by failures or become even stronger as a result.

I am right-handed, so learning to spin the nunchaku with my left hand was difficult. I hit my forearm thousands of times. My skin was red after just one hour of practice. People asked me why I kept trying and why I did not give up. The reason I continued was my enthusiasm for mastering the nunchaku. After months of practice, I succeeded. I am not a master yet, but at least I no longer hit myself.

Many people who face repeated failures also risk reaching a point where they cannot try again. This could mean a failure that results in death, though not all failures are that extreme. There are situations where a person becomes unable to do something they once could do. However, there are also cases where people become stronger after tragedy. There was a boy who loved riding his bicycle and performing tricks. One day, he was in an accident with a car and lost his leg. He spent months in a wheelchair, but doctors gave him an artificial leg. He spent a lot of time recovering, and when he was able to move independently, he wanted to return to his passion. For a long time, he failed to do anything with his bike. He felt angry and broken. But he did not give up. After failing again and again, he finally rode his bike again. Today, he rides just like before the accident because he never surrendered. His story inspires me.

We need a goal that keeps us enthusiastic and prevents us from losing motivation, making us stronger after every failure. We can stay in our comfort zones and avoid failure, or we can face it and gain valuable experience.

Many responsibilities exist in life that we must fulfill, and with these duties come challenges that humans must overcome in various ways. The city council is currently considering implementing a 10PM weekday curfew and a midnight curfew for teenagers. I appreciate that the council is taking this matter seriously, but I disagree with these proposed restrictions for several important reasons.

Teenagers often have obligations after school, including extracurricular activities and part-time jobs. Additionally, traffic congestion can cause significant delays, making it difficult to return home at specific times. I understand the reasoning behind concerns about teenagers driving at night, as exhaustion can certainly affect concentration and alertness. However, teenagers are often capable of staying awake much longer than adults. This is not because we are simply bored or wasting time; rather, we stay up to demonstrate that we can handle responsibilities and manage our own schedules. Many of us work evening jobs and remain awake until we return home because we are genuinely capable of taking care of ourselves.

That said, I do believe teenagers should be off the roads before midnight. This is primarily because individuals who are under the influence of alcohol or drugs tend to be on the roads during late-night hours. Additionally, depending on the area, there may be wildlife such as deer that pose dangers to drivers. The nighttime presents many hazards that are difficult to see, and there are also potentially dangerous people who might cause harm. Furthermore, even experienced drivers can become fatigued after a long day and risk getting into accidents.

In conclusion, I understand why the council is concerned about teenagers driving at 10PM or past midnight due to the various dangers that exist after dark. However, I hope the council recognizes that we do not stay awake for trivial reasons. We are often occupied with important matters such as work or school-related activities, and we will be cautious while driving at night because we are aware of the risks involved.

Some individuals may have valid concerns about attending school in person, such as difficulties with social interactions or personal circumstances that make learning from home more suitable. While I would personally prefer going to school to interact with others, I understand why many students choose online education.

Here are three reasons explaining why students might prefer online classes from home.

The first reason relates to social discomfort. Some students do not feel comfortable around others, believing that people can be unkind, disrespectful, or judgmental. Additionally, parents may worry about how their children will be treated by peers or fear negative influences that could lead their children down the wrong path. Furthermore, some families are concerned about medical conditions that might cause others to mock or ridicule their children.

The second reason involves personal preferences and emotional well-being. Certain students simply prefer the comfort of their own home environment. They may feel anxious about facing others daily or worry about being judged. Some students have experienced embarrassing situations at school in the past, making them reluctant to return to a traditional classroom setting.

The third reason reflects my own perspective. If I had to choose between online learning and attending school, I would select in-person classes. I believe that school provides valuable opportunities to meet new people and make connections. I would also want to encourage others who feel ashamed of their problems to understand that they should not let negative comments affect them. Bullies often do not consider the harm they cause to others.

In conclusion, students should have the freedom to choose online education if they have legitimate reasons for preferring it. However, I also believe that people should not be overly concerned about what others think or say about them.

Do you believe that experiencing failure is necessary to achieve success in life? In my opinion, I strongly agree with this idea. I think failure is essential because it helps us become more confident, prepares us for the real world, and teaches us that we must fight for what we want in life.

My mother always encouraged me by saying, "Believe in yourself; I know you can do it." When I was in first grade in Honduras, one of my teachers told my mother that I was struggling with mathematics and would probably fail the year. Unfortunately, she was right. However, my mother didn't criticize me. Instead, she told me that failing didn't mean I wasn't intelligent—it simply meant the subject was difficult for me, but she knew I could overcome it. The following year, I had to repeat first grade, and that experience was completely different. My teacher told my mother that I had improved remarkably in math and all my other subjects. I am grateful for that failure because it taught me that failing once doesn't mean giving up; it means fighting back, which is exactly what I did.

I have always told myself to never give up on my dreams, no matter how challenging things become. When I was younger, I dreamed of becoming a lawyer. During a school activity where we had to share our future aspirations, I announced that I wanted to be a lawyer. One of my classmates mocked me, saying, "How could you become a lawyer? You'll never complete that degree." I responded confidently, "You never know. No matter how many times I fail, I will keep trying." I believe that if you don't fight for your dreams, you are allowing yourself to become a failure, and I refuse to be that person. I will never let anyone else determine what I can or cannot achieve.

Failing once or multiple times doesn't mean you will never succeed—it actually means the opposite. Throughout my eighteen years of life, I have experienced many failures. I believe that implementing a curfew for teenagers is a positive step forward and should be introduced for several important reasons. First, during weekdays young people have school every day unless it's a holiday or they are unwell. With a curfew in place, fewer teenagers will be wandering the streets late at night, which is unnecessary in the first place.

Second, ten o'clock in the evening is an appropriate time for young people to be home on weekdays. This will help keep them away from trouble and reduce their chances of becoming victims of criminals who operate at night. Most criminal activities occur after dark, so implementing a curfew would significantly decrease these risks.

Third, given the prevalence of drug dealers in many areas, if young people are required to return home early, their exposure to various drugs and dangerous substances will be greatly reduced. This alone makes the curfew worthwhile.

The proposed times seem reasonable. Monday through Friday until ten p.m., and weekends until midnight, give young people plenty of flexibility. No one really needs to be on the streets later than these hours. If someone is out past the designated time, there should be a serious justification for breaking the law.

This curfew would primarily keep young people out of additional trouble. The hours provided are quite generous and should not interfere significantly with anyone's life. Teenagers can still go out and socialize, just not until the early morning hours.

I understand that some people might prefer this law to apply to adults as well, since young adults enjoy parties and nightlife. However, it makes more sense to restrict those under eighteen, as they are still developing and may not always make the best decisions. Once someone turns eighteen, they are considered adults and should know the difference between right and wrong.

This legislation is not designed to harm anyone but rather to improve communities by keeping teenagers safe. However, if young people choose to engage in inappropriate behavior, no law will completely change their actions. The curfew simply provides a structure to encourage better choices.

It's important to note that this law does not prevent teenagers from spending time with their friends. It simply aims to keep them safer from the dangers that lurk on the streets late at night. Many innocent people become victims of crime simply because they were out too late. Teenagers have plenty of time after school for activities and socializing.

There should be some exceptions allowed, such as attending parties, but even then, reasonable limits should exist. Consequences for violating the curfew should begin with a warning before escalating to more serious penalties.

I can understand why some people oppose this idea, but teenagers generally know what they should and should not be doing. There are two perspectives to consider. On one hand, some worry about activities like sleepovers - would those be permitted, or must teenagers be specifically at home? On the other hand, if a teenager attends a party on the weekend and loses track of time, returning home at one in the morning, they could face legal consequences. This could result in a record that follows them, potentially affecting their future college applications. Colleges thoroughly examine applicants' backgrounds, and even a minor violation could impact their chances of acceptance. This is certainly a downside worth considering.

Currently, there is no curfew for teenagers regarding their whereabouts, but there are restrictions on when permit holders can drive. This means young people are rarely seen out late at night, except immediately after school.

There are advantages and disadvantages to this proposed law, but the benefits outweigh the drawbacks. Everything seems quite reasonable and understandable. The main concern I have is the possibility of a violation appearing on someone's record, which could have lasting negative effects.

Overall, this curfew should be implemented across the entire United States, not just in individual cities. It would keep more people safe. Of course, there will always be individuals who break the law as a joke, but this is a serious matter that all young people should take seriously.

In conclusion, this curfew would help prevent criminals from targeting young boys and girls, and could reduce incidents of other serious crimes that often occur under the cover of darkness. Most importantly, it would keep teenagers away from dangerous situations and the various risks associated with being out late at night.

These include shortened learning periods, teachers receiving hourly wages instead of stable salaries, and potential negative effects on the economy.

In my opinion, school hours should not be shortened simply to conserve energy. Students need to attend school for approximately eight hours daily. Without sufficient time in the classroom, teachers cannot cover all the required curriculum material. Additionally, students' academic progress would suffer greatly if they only attended for two hours per week.

Another concern is that educators would transition from receiving monthly salaries to being paid by the hour. This would result in considerably lower compensation. Many people wonder whether confidence develops from accomplishing goals or whether it must exist beforehand to enable success. Some believe that students need self-assurance in order to learn effectively, while others argue that self-esteem is the result of achieving something. In my view, confidence must come before accomplishment, because believing in yourself is essential for working hard, completing tasks, and overcoming fear.

First, individuals need self-confidence in order to put in effort and continue learning new skills. For example, doctors never stop studying because new illnesses and treatments are constantly emerging. Similarly, learning a foreign language like English when you already speak Spanish can be extremely challenging. Some English words have multiple meanings, and certain concepts don't even exist in both languages. Even native speakers do not know every single word in their language. However, by maintaining confidence in your abilities, you can accept that learning is an ongoing process and feel proud of the progress you make each day.

Second, having confidence and a positive attitude is necessary for accomplishing tasks. When people feel angry or anxious, they cannot focus properly, which leads to poor results. During exam periods, students often feel overwhelmed and unprepared. The self-assurance they have built up by attending classes regularly and doing their homework is what helps them retain information and perform well under pressure. If you have studied consistently, you will feel ready when the testing day arrives.

Third, confidence means believing in yourself before attempting something new. When applying for a job, you may feel uncertain about how the interview will go or how you will be received. You must let your confidence overcome your fears, because fear prevents you from taking action. During that first meeting, the employers need to see that you are capable of doing the job. They will not hire someone who appears unsure of their own abilities.

Nevertheless, some people argue that self-esteem comes from achievement. They believe that accomplishing something brings satisfaction and confidence as a reward. For instance, passing a difficult test or exam can make students feel proud of their efforts. After working hard for months to prepare for important examinations, the relief of finally completing them brings happiness and a sense of accomplishment. In the same way, passing a driving test on the first attempt can boost someone's confidence significantly, making them feel they can tackle other challenges. Additionally, positive thinkers tend to believe everything will work out well, and this mindset helps them persist until they succeed. Learning any new skill involves struggle at first, but those who trust in their ability to improve will eventually master it.

Despite these points, I still believe that confidence must come before achievement. Confidence provides the courage to face challenges and the determination to keep trying despite difficulties. Without belief in oneself, no effort would be made in the first place. Therefore, my advice is to trust in yourself and your capabilities. Let confidence replace fear, and success will follow. When you achieve your goals, the fear will disappear, and your confidence will remain strong.

In my opinion, working in a group is much better than working alone. There are several reasons why I believe group work is preferable. First of all, assignments get completed much faster when multiple people are working together. Secondly, each person can focus on a different part of the task, which makes the whole process more efficient. Thirdly, group members can help each other when someone is struggling with their section.

Of course, there are some disadvantages to working in a group. For example, there can be many distractions, and sometimes people have different ideas about how the assignment should look. Now, let me discuss the benefits of working alone. The main advantage is that there are no distractions getting in the way. Additionally, you only have to consider your own ideas, and you can ask the teacher directly for clarification, which means the work will be done exactly as requested. However, the negative side of working alone is that it takes much longer to finish, and you have to do everything by yourself without any support.

In the end, whether you choose to work in a group or alone, you will face similar challenges. You will still need to complete the same amount of work, and you will still have to deal with different ideas about how the assignment should be done. For me, I would definitely prefer to work in a group because I know that if I work alone, I probably will not finish my assignment on time. In a group, I only need to complete my specific part, which is much more manageable. Some might say that I am choosing group work to do less work, and they would be right. However, the important thing is that the work gets done rather than not being completed at all. Therefore, for my conclusion, I prefer working in a group rather than working alone because, as the saying goes, "teamwork makes the dream work."

While working independently may present more challenges than collaborating with others, it ultimately provides greater opportunities for genuine learning. Whether we work alone or in a team, we are still completing tasks and gaining knowledge along the way. However, the process of discovering information yourself, particularly when working alone, tends to be more valuable than simply relying on group members' contributions.

When I emphasize learning, I mean actually understanding material rather than just finishing assignments. In group settings, everyone brings their own ideas and knowledge about the subject, which can be helpful. Unfortunately, many individuals take advantage of group work to simply copy answers from others without putting in any real effort. Copying does not contribute to genuine understanding; it only results in completed work.

I believe working alone is more beneficial for my learning process. Admittedly, it takes longer to finish tasks when I work independently because I invest time in exploring small details and verifying information. Some people prefer not to work alone, but this is my preferred approach. One advantage of individual work is the satisfaction you feel upon completion. When you accomplish something without relying on others, except for receiving the initial instructions, you can take genuine pride in your achievement.

Group work is not inherently negative, but I believe students and professionals would benefit from developing independent work skills. The reason is that working alone forces you to actually learn the material rather than just getting it done. In groups, some members simply copy from others who have finished their portions. While not everyone engages in this behavior, many students do take advantage of group work to avoid doing their own work. Others genuinely collaborate and share completed portions with teammates. Working together can be easier than working alone, but independent work offers superior learning benefits.

People who are unaccustomed to working independently may feel uncomfortable when first assigned individual tasks because they are accustomed to relying on others. Working alone encourages individuals to push themselves to discover additional details, facts, and evidence for their work. Of course, if someone struggles, they can always ask a teacher or colleague for assistance. Working independently also allows for better concentration. In group settings, conversations and the exchange of ideas can become distracting, making it difficult to maintain focus on your own work.

Additionally, other people's ideas within a group may contain errors, and if you use those ideas in your own work, you become incorrect as well. Furthermore, group communication can be difficult for some people, which makes independent work preferable. When working alone, you can complete tasks using your own methods and reasoning. These points demonstrate why independent work is more advantageous for learning than group collaboration.

Expressing gratitude through simple words like thank you or you're welcome makes a significant difference in our daily interactions. When we speak kindly to others and demonstrate good manners, we create a positive atmosphere around us. Being thankful for what people do for us, whether they give us something or simply help us out, should become a natural habit. These small gestures matter because they encourage others to respond in the same way.

When we treat others with kindness and courtesy, they tend to reciprocate those behaviors. If we say thank you or offer polite responses, others will likely do the same for us. This creates a cycle of mutual respect and consideration. Developing good manners is essential for any situation we encounter in life. Using respectful language such as yes sir or thank you demonstrates our upbringing and consideration for others. However, this works both ways - if we want others to show us respect, we must first demonstrate it ourselves.

Having good manners also helps us build new friendships. When we express appreciation after someone assists us or does something thoughtful, we strengthen our connections with them. Speaking kindly to others can brighten their day, and we never know how much our words might mean to someone. Being friendly and courteous is the foundation of lasting relationships.

While it is not mandatory to always use formal manners, developing them certainly benefits us. When we hurt someone's feelings, offering a sincere apology and kind words helps repair the situation. People are more likely to be respectful towards us when we show respect to them first. Those who lack basic courtesy often find it difficult to maintain positive relationships with others.

Demonstrating kindness and good manners reveals positive aspects of our character. When we go shopping or visit establishments, we should ask service workers how their day is going. Making them feel valued creates a pleasant experience for everyone involved. Even when someone simply wishes us a good day, responding with thank you and wishing them well in return shows our appreciation and warmth.

When dining at restaurants, expressing gratitude and perhaps leaving a tip are excellent ways to show kindness to staff members. If we notice someone having a difficult day, offering assistance or kind words can make a meaningful difference in their situation.

The bottom line is that our words and actions shape how others treat us. The more we demonstrate courtesy and kindness, the more we receive in return. When others compliment us or speak positively to us, responding in kind strengthens our relationships. Cultivating good manners ultimately leads to a more harmonious and fulfilling life for everyone involved.

However, if you are taking an online course, it becomes much harder to understand the main idea of the lesson. We do not have a teacher sitting next to us. Honestly, you do learn to be more organized and independent, but I still believe students should attend classes at school. Doing online work and taking so many notes is not ideal.

This should not happen when taking online classes because there is still a purpose and responsibility. The question of whether schools should regulate students' participation in extracurricular activities remains a subject of ongoing discussion. Some individuals argue that educational institutions should have control over how students spend their time outside the classroom, believing that structured activities would enhance academic learning. However, I contend that students should be free to make their own choices regarding their after-school time. This is because many students need to work to support their families, others must care for their siblings at home, and some prefer to engage in activities like sports or arts based on their personal interests.

To begin with, numerous students are required to work part-time jobs to contribute to their family's income. Balancing employment with academic responsibilities can be extremely challenging. After a long day of work, students often feel exhausted and simply want to rest. Those who work while studying frequently struggle to find time for homework, test preparation, or school projects. While study halls can provide some assistance with assignments, these working students typically cannot participate in extracurricular activities due to their demanding schedules. Many students work to save money for their future college education, which represents a responsible investment in their long-term goals. Consequently, students with jobs must prioritize their work commitments over additional school activities.

Furthermore, some students face significant family responsibilities that limit their availability for extracurricular involvement. Many children must return home promptly to supervise their younger siblings because their parents work long hours and cannot afford childcare services. These students often manage household tasks like preparing meals, cleaning, and doing laundry while caring for their brothers and sisters. Juggling schoolwork with family obligations creates considerable challenges, leaving little time for extracurricular engagement.

On the other hand, many students genuinely enjoy participating in various activities according to their individual preferences. Some are passionate about athletics and want to exercise daily, choosing from sports such as basketball, baseball, tennis, or gymnastics. Others prefer creative pursuits, environmental causes, or learning new languages by joining appropriate school clubs. These students are more than willing to take part in extracurricular activities, but the specific choice should remain theirs to make rather than being imposed by the school.

In conclusion, students deserve autonomy in determining how they spend their time beyond regular school hours. Each individual faces unique circumstances, whether working to support their family, caring for siblings, or pursuing personal passions. When we understand and respect these different situations, we create a more understanding and supportive educational environment for everyone.

Should Students Choose a Career Early?

In certain societies, students are expected to decide on their future profession before they even start high school. However, the important question is whether this is actually beneficial for young people.

I believe that choosing a career at a young age can be advantageous for students who are interested in professions that require many years of study, such as medicine, law, or teaching. If young people begin preparing for these fields early, they can contribute significantly to their country's development in the future.

Additionally, when students start their career path at a young age, they have greater flexibility to continue or even change direction later. For instance, if a teacher decides to pursue a different profession, they can do so because they are still young and have the energy to adapt.

Nevertheless, there are also some drawbacks to consider. Students might become exhausted from spending so many years in education. They may also regret their initial choice and realize years later that the career they selected does not actually suit them.

In conclusion, I believe that committing to a career at a young age is a positive approach for students. That is why teachers and counselors should provide guidance and support to help young people find the right career path for their lives. With proper encouragement, students can make informed decisions about their future.

Student Choice Leads to Better Summer Projects

Summer assignments can be enjoyable, but only if students have the freedom to select their own topics. When learners are permitted to choose projects based on their interests, they become more engaged, put forth greater effort, and actually enjoy the work.

Teachers invest considerable time developing project ideas for students to complete during breaks. However, many students fail to dedicate much thought or energy to these assigned tasks. This represents a waste of the teacher's effort. In contrast, when students create their own topics and concepts, they are far more likely to complete the work thoroughly.

If students select their own projects, they will probably finish them because they involve subjects they genuinely want to learn about. When learners are curious about something, they tend to explore that interest and become more involved in the material. Students can develop excellent ideas when working on personal projects. Selecting a topic that interests them allows students to expand their thinking and accomplish things they never imagined possible.

Summer projects can also enhance grades in a particular subject. For instance, a student who struggles in class due to an inability to keep up with the pace can benefit from working independently during summer break. Additionally, students who perform poorly in crowded classroom environments get an opportunity for self-directed study. Summer projects provide a chance for learners to improve their achievements. When students choose their own assignments, they can work at a speed that suits them without worrying about strict deadlines. They have the entire summer to complete their work, and if they fail to finish despite having all that time, that simply reflects laziness and could negatively impact their grades.

The subject matter significantly affects student motivation. When a student receives an assignment on a topic they dislike, they are likely to procrastinate or avoid doing it altogether. Consequently, they will have no interest in completing the summer assignment. For example, if I were assigned a history project and a science project, and my science teacher asked me to write a research paper about gene mutation, no matter how intriguing it sounds, I would not complete it because science does not fascinate me the way history does.

Having the ability to choose one's own project can be enjoyable because it gives students something to look forward to and makes them more enthusiastic about their work. Students should design their own summer projects because this approach reduces the workload for teachers, provides learners with an opportunity to think creatively beyond their usual boundaries, and enables them to make their teachers proud by completing quality work. This positive experience can lead to anticipating a better upcoming school year.

While some individuals believe that sticking with what they already know helps them reach their objectives, others argue that taking on more difficult tasks allows them to exceed those goals.

Reaching beyond your original objectives can propel you further in life, make your career or hobbies more engaging, and broaden your knowledge. If you think you cannot accomplish something, you are simply not trusting in your own abilities.

To succeed and find satisfaction, you must first have confidence in yourself. Push yourself to do more than you initially thought possible.

Advancement in life is closely tied to your surroundings, the people around you, and the effort you put in. In my view, progressing in life is valuable since not everyone has the same opportunities.

Consider the example of a student who decided to take a chemistry course despite her doubts. At first, she believed she would fail, but in the end, she passed the class successfully. Do not settle for less than you deserve.

Some people dislike their work, which leads them to perform poorly. However, making your job enjoyable is possible. How can you achieve this? First, identify something you genuinely enjoy. People generally enjoy games because they present challenges, and this mindset can transform your approach to any task.

There are countless ways to gain knowledge. Be prepared for any situation that arises, both mentally and emotionally, and even physically.

Life is full of unexpected events that teach us both positive and negative lessons over time. Simply do your best and learn from everything that occurs or will occur in the future.

Some schools implement programs where older students mentor younger ones. The older students assist with various activities or homework assignments. But how does this arrangement benefit both groups? I believe this program is advantageous for several important reasons.

The first benefit is that younger students receive valuable support from their older peers. Since older students possess more knowledge and experience, they can provide meaningful assistance with schoolwork. If the program continues to grow, more students will participate and may even form study groups where they work together on different tasks.

Secondly, this program can significantly help students who are struggling academically. Those receiving low grades or poor test scores can benefit greatly from additional one-on-one support. Furthermore, students can contribute by donating school supplies such as binders, books, folders, crayons, pencils, pens, and paper. They could also organize fundraising events like bake sales to raise money for materials.

Finally, this program proves valuable not only for individual students but also for the wider community. When younger students receive guidance and support, they develop better study habits and confidence. Older students also gain by reinforcing their own knowledge and learning responsibility.

In conclusion, pairing older students with younger students through mentoring programs creates mutual benefits. This initiative deserves continued support and expansion.

Living in a world that constantly pushes us to become someone other than ourselves raises an important question: is it difficult to remain authentic in a society that demands conformity? Throughout our lives, we find ourselves attempting to blend in with others rather than embracing our true identities. In this essay, I will discuss how society continuously attempts to reshape us, the various ways we become influenced by our surroundings, and the concerning direction in which younger generations seem to be heading.

Modern society is always searching for methods to alter our thinking and behavior. As individuals, we should pause and reflect on what we genuinely desire for our futures. Why should we strive to be identical to everyone else? Are we pursuing wealth and status within this society? Do we wish to achieve our personal ambitions? These are essential questions we must ask ourselves. We should consider where we will end up if we simply follow the crowd. In today's world, success requires authenticity; the world will not hand us achievement on a silver platter.

We are heavily influenced by society in numerous ways, including our activities, communication styles, fashion choices, and even religious beliefs. If we fail to follow current trends or popular styles, we risk being judged as uncool. Consider fashion, for instance. If we do not wear the latest clothing or most popular shoes, society may view us as unfashionable or unattractive. The reasons for not wearing these items might include financial constraints, lack of time, or simply personal preference. However, society often overlooks these realities and judges people harshly. This superficial judgment can lead to bullying and even depression among those who cannot afford trendy items, which is truly unfortunate.

Unfortunately, each passing year finds our younger generations becoming increasingly problematic, largely due to societal influences. We have been negatively affected by emerging drugs that claim lives, ongoing conflicts between nations, and new musicians who create songs about drugs, violence, and inappropriate content. These elements pose serious threats to young people. If we do not begin to assert our individuality and prioritize positive choices, we risk heading toward a troubling future.

Some individuals claim that the world is inherently evil and provides only negative influences. However, this perspective overlooks an important truth. The world itself is not solely responsible; we also bear accountability for allowing ourselves to be drawn into harmful situations. It is easy to blame external factors when we make poor choices, but ultimately, we must accept responsibility for our own decisions. I remain hopeful that our world can transform for the better. We still possess the opportunity to create meaningful change, and it is not an impossible task. I trust that upcoming generations will find the courage to improve our world and establish a more compassionate and welcoming society for everyone.

I strongly believe that maintaining a positive mindset is essential for achieving success in life. Having a good outlook in any professional environment is crucial, and you never hear someone with a negative attitude being celebrated at any gathering. In all honesty, carrying a positive attitude wherever you go can benefit you greatly.

I agree not only because a good attitude feels nice, but also because it can make others smile and push away negative energy. I feel fortunate to naturally possess a cheerful outlook. Additionally, bringing a positive attitude to work can make your day go by much faster, allowing you to return home and relax comfortably. I work at a restaurant, and I've noticed that when I have a negative mindset, time seems to crawl. However, when I approach my shift with optimism, the hours fly by quickly.

Your attitude also forms part of your first impression on others, which can benefit you greatly in the long term. It can instantly transform a difficult situation into a favorable one, which is truly valuable.

Furthermore, I believe that bringing positivity to the workplace can lead to numerous opportunities in the future. You might meet your future partner or encounter successful individuals who could influence your life positively. Many people fail to realize how maintaining a positive rather than negative outlook can work to their advantage. A good attitude can take you to places others never imagined, helping you achieve success such as securing a good job, earning promotions, reaching the top of your field, and accumulating wealth. Many people aspire to become wealthy and successful, yet not everyone is willing to cultivate a positive attitude. Everyone has their own beliefs and perspectives about life.

Unfortunately, many people in this world tend to be negative. Some face tremendous hardships and struggle because they lack resources or purpose. However, this mindset is counterproductive. No matter what challenges arise, individuals must remain hopeful and keep moving forward.

Additionally, I believe that being kind to others and offering a smile can brighten many people's days, making the world a more pleasant place and helping everyone appreciate what they have. Humans are social beings who prefer companionship rather than isolation. They genuinely want the best for one another. Honestly, people should strive to create better work environments while maintaining positive attitudes.

Having a good attitude is extremely beneficial in the workplace and beyond. People should understand what is best for them and prioritize their well-being. While I imagine many individuals with positive attitudes existing, there are unfortunately just as many who carry negative ones.

Is having a positive mindset truly essential for achieving success in life? In my view, maintaining a positive attitude is vital because it can help us succeed at work, motivate us to give our best effort even during challenging times, improve our relationships, and help us believe in ourselves.

Let me share some experiences that demonstrate why I believe positive thinking is so important. While working at a restaurant called Mango Paradise, my manager was often bitter and quick to anger. However, I chose not to let his negative behavior affect me. I always stayed cheerful and approached my work with a smile, regardless of how he treated the team. One particular day, my boss was clearly distressed because a family member was seriously ill in the hospital. His wife had cancer, and she was in critical condition. I approached him and asked if we could talk. I wanted to offer my support and let him know that we were all there for him during this difficult time. Unfortunately, his wife eventually passed away. Throughout that terrible period, our team stayed positive and kept reassuring him that everything would be okay, that his wife was now at peace and no longer suffering. My father was devastated and spent months searching for employment without success. Like any supportive partner, my mother encouraged him and said, "Do not worry, sweetheart. We will get through this together, just like we always do. I am here for you." My father's attitude changed almost immediately. He smiled at my mother, thanked her for her faith in him, grabbed his car keys, and went out to search for work again. Eventually, he found a new job that paid even better than his previous one. Seeking Guidance: One Person or Many

In my opinion, consulting several individuals for advice proves more advantageous than relying on a single source. I once came across a quote from LeBron James that emphasized the importance of gathering multiple perspectives. The reasoning behind this makes perfect sense to me - one person might provide accurate guidance while another could be mistaken. Therefore, there is absolutely no harm in reaching out to several people you respect and admire.

However, I understand that some individuals prefer not to engage with many people. In such cases, selecting just one trustworthy person becomes essential. If you do decide to consult only one individual, you must ensure that this person is wise and consistently makes sound decisions. Personally, I would approach someone who has demonstrated good judgment and life experience, as their insights would help me avoid poor choices. The key is choosing the right person - someone who will offer valuable feedback rather than misleading information.

There are definite advantages to seeking advice from a single individual as well. When sharing sensitive or personal matters, confiding in one person reduces the risk of your information spreading. If you tell numerous people your private business, rumors could circulate and you might even become a target for bullying. For confidential matters, keeping it between yourself and one trusted person is often the wiser approach. Additionally, school counselors represent excellent resources because they are professionally bound to maintain confidentiality and often have the experience to understand your situation.

Regardless of whether you choose one person or several, seeking advice can always prove beneficial. Nevertheless, you must exercise caution in your selection. Asking someone who consistently makes poor decisions for guidance would be unwise, as they would likely encourage you to follow their negative patterns. This could potentially lead you down a troubled path.

In conclusion, advice has the power to significantly impact people's lives - for better or worse. The quality of guidance you receive depends entirely on whom you choose to ask.

Should Students Prepare for Their Future Careers While in High School?

In this essay, I will argue that students should take classes that prepare them for their future careers while they are still in high school. Starting to think about career paths at a young age is important because it helps young people avoid ending up with unfulfilling and low-paying jobs when they become adults.

I am currently in the eleventh grade, and I already know what I want to be when I grow up. I want to become a United States Marine soldier. The classes I am taking right now in high school will help me achieve this goal. One of these classes is JROTC, which stands for Junior Reserve Officers' Training Corps. This program teaches students about the United States Armed Forces and helps them develop discipline and leadership skills that are valuable in military careers.

Another class I am taking that will benefit my future is Economics. While this course is required for graduation at my school, I appreciate it because I understand that financial knowledge will be useful throughout my life, regardless of the career path I choose.

If we do not start preparing ourselves for our future careers after high school, we may feel lost, confused, and struggle financially. In my family, I do not think anyone was able to pursue what they truly wanted to do. My mother once told me that she dreamed of becoming an artist, but she never achieved this goal because her school did not offer art classes, and she eventually dropped out to start a family. This shows how the lack of career preparation opportunities can negatively affect people's lives.

Work is something that everyone must do at some point in their lives. Therefore, I believe it is a wise idea to begin discovering what we would enjoy doing as adults while we are still in high school. When I grow up, I want to serve as a United States Marine, and I am confident that the classes I am taking today will help me reach that goal.

From a person that lived this before at a young age.

I believe Ralph Waldo Emerson was absolutely right when he wrote this, and most people would agree. It is similar to the situation where someone goes to college, gets a degree, and then returns to live with their parents. They could move out, find a job, save money, and eventually buy their own house. However, if they continue living with their parents, nothing really changes. Their parents will continue treating them like a little child until they start getting their own things, regardless of how old they actually are. Parents tend to see their children the same way they did when they were born.

For the rest of society, a person becomes a grown man or woman when they get their life together. This means having their own car, house, and family to take care of. They will do anything for their family, just like their parents did for them. It becomes the same story but from a different perspective. The person who is now telling the story will never want their children to grow up. They will always look at them as their children, no matter how old those children become.

I did not fully understand this until I saw my older sister taking care of her daughter. That was when I started looking at life from a different perspective. I may not be completely grown up yet, but I moved out of my house when I was fifteen. I thought it would be difficult to keep up with the rest of the world. I believe that before you can take your own path and stop worrying about what others think, that is when you really grow up. Family comes first, second, and third.

I think the best way to grow is to do things for yourself. There is no need to move out if that is not possible. You simply need to look at the rest of the world from a different side. That is when you really grow. It is not about age or anything like that. It is about not worrying about anyone besides your family and your friends.

Online learning programs offered by schools can bring both advantages and disadvantages. Every educational institution handles this differently, as some provide such options while others do not. People also hold varying opinions about this approach. Some believe it is beneficial, while others consider it problematic. One advantage of virtual classrooms is that students do not need to wait for others to finish. They can proceed at their own speed and complete assignments according to their schedule. However, there are also significant drawbacks to consider. Internet connections may become slow or fail completely. Students might struggle to complete their assignments. They miss the experience of being in a different environment surrounded by peers of similar age. Additionally, some learners simply fail to submit their work on time.

When students attend classes online, they often find it difficult to complete the tasks assigned to them. They cannot directly ask questions about problems they encounter. They must solve everything independently. Some online resources do not provide the help students need. They might offer incorrect information, which could result in students getting entire assignments wrong. Tutorial videos may exist, but sometimes there are very few available for specific topics. In a traditional classroom, students could request the teacher to demonstrate solutions, making understanding much easier. With online learning, teachers are not always accessible when assistance is required. Furthermore, many students fail to submit their work by deadlines. They tend to postpone tasks, telling themselves they will complete them later, but often never do. Meeting deadlines becomes a real challenge.

Interacting with same-age peers offers important benefits. Students can form study groups and request help from classmates. In online education, learners work mostly alone with their computer and course materials. Even if they have friends, those friends might not be enrolled in the same classes, preventing collaboration or joint studying. Online students often have limited opportunities to socialize with new people. They may be occupied with work or other responsibilities, and the people around them tend to be older, or they simply do not engage in much conversation. A different environment can enhance learning, and being accompanied by others in the same room proves valuable. Students should not be isolated at home with only a computer for company. Virtual classes often mean studying without companions of similar age.

Online classes sometimes assign substantial amounts of work to be completed within a single day. This becomes challenging when students do not comprehend the material or simply cannot follow along. Completing assignments properly is essential for understanding the course content. Students should not simply search online for something that resembles their work and copy it down. Many learners become lazy and neglect their responsibilities. They often wait until the last minute to submit anything. This laziness can lead to poor grades or even failure, requiring students to retake the entire course. Students can easily become distracted by other aspects of their lives. Failing to complete work will not help them progress, and they may miss deadlines.

Educational institutions provide various options for students, whether online or in physical classrooms. This flexibility can benefit learners by allowing them to attend more classes and enjoy additional free time. However, some students might misuse this opportunity by staying home without actually studying. Life can be difficult, and unexpected situations arise. When students do not understand the material and no teacher is available to assist them, they face significant challenges. Students must make choices that serve their best interests. Online learning can be difficult to manage. Students may lack interaction with peers their own age and may fail to complete their work. Virtual education does not always work well for every student.

I believe that schools should establish after-school homework clubs because many students find homework difficult to complete when they lack proper guidance. When learners do not fully grasp the material, they often feel confused about what they are supposed to do. If such clubs existed, consider how much work students would be able to finish successfully.

Some people may question the importance of homework, but it actually contributes around ten percent to one's final grade. While this percentage might seem small, it could make a significant difference between passing and failing. Furthermore, completing homework prepares students for upcoming tests and quizzes. That assignment you skipped might have contained exactly the information needed to pass that difficult test you failed.

Additionally, many pupils struggle to understand the work their teachers assign. If a student did not comprehend the lesson in class, how can they be expected to complete homework on that same topic? This creates frustration and discouragement.

Middle school students face particular challenges because they must manage assignments from seven different subjects simultaneously. Some teachers assign two or three pieces of homework, making the workload even more overwhelming.

After-school homework clubs would allow students to ask questions about anything they do not understand. Teachers could clarify concepts that were confusing during regular class time. For students who simply lack adequate time at home due to family responsibilities or other obligations, staying after school provides an opportunity to get work done. Importantly, these clubs would teach students rather than simply providing ready-made answers. This approach helps learners genuinely understand the material.

Improved homework completion would also boost students' grades, potentially raising a B to an A. The school itself would benefit reputation-wise if more students submitted quality work. Teachers would know that pupils were completing assignments thoughtfully rather than copying answers from classmates. Additionally, students who understand the material but struggle with deadlines would greatly benefit from this extra time.

In conclusion, an after-school homework club would be highly valuable. Homework represents a significant challenge in many schools, and numerous students fail to recognize how much it matters. They may wonder why they failed an exam or quiz when the answer could be as simple as not completing the assigned work. Teachers assign homework to help students improve in their subjects. Some learners dismiss homework as unimportant, but this mindset does not change the reality that it affects their success. No matter how often someone tells themselves it does not matter, it actually does.

If such a club were implemented, homework would become one less thing to worry about. Students would feel less stressed about their workloads and would finally understand their assignments properly. Once homework is finished, they could enjoy their afternoons without anxiety. Knowing they have completed their responsibilities would allow them to relax and participate in other activities they value.

While some concepts may seem challenging to implement alone, working collectively makes it possible to overcome difficulties and reach common goals.

Furthermore, teamwork enables groups to succeed in competitions. Each person plays a specific role and contributes their unique skills. Some members perform on stage while others provide support behind the scenes. Everyone rehearses together and dedicates time to ensure the group performs at its best, even if it means spending less time with family during preparation periods.

Finally, entertaining the audience represents a crucial goal for any group. Spectators attend events hoping to enjoy themselves, so group members must work diligently to engage and delight them. Having a clear leader who assigns responsibilities and coordinates timing helps create more dynamic and interactive performances.

In conclusion, I believe that collaborative work leads to better outcomes. Teams can develop creative ideas, produce entertaining shows, and bring happiness to their audience. When group members, families, and teachers witness their combined efforts, they feel proud of what has been accomplished. Working together is truly more rewarding and enjoyable.

Many people nowadays spend more time on social media through their devices than actually talking to others face to face. Research shows that those who use technology excessively for long periods often experience depression and other mental health issues. We should reduce the time we spend on technology for entertainment purposes. This could lead to healthier lives and help protect our eyesight from needing glasses. One of my close friends started wearing glasses when he was only five years old because he spent too much time watching television.

Of course, technology does have some practical uses. It allows us to send photos to family members who live far away, complete homework assignments, check the time, and stay in contact with friends and relatives in other countries. However, technology can be quite expensive, and in my opinion, it does not truly benefit us in meaningful ways. Excessive screen time can actually harm our brain function.

Technology can also make people less intelligent. For example, if someone spends all their time on their phone instead of studying for an exam, they will likely receive poor grades. This demonstrates how technology can be harmful to everyone. Using technology too much can damage brain cells. I know someone who cheated on a test using his phone while the teacher sat at his desk, also distracted by his own phone. Unfortunately, some teachers behave this way as well.

Not all teachers are like this, but some certainly are. Even during physical education classes, many students simply sit and play on their phones rather than participating. Personally, I prefer to play sports like soccer, baseball, and basketball, with soccer being my favorite.

I am referring to students, and even gym teachers sometimes use their phones too. The point is that this problem exists everywhere, every day. Am I the only one who has noticed this? These things happen constantly, in every place. Did you just realize it?

Ralph Waldo Emerson once said that being yourself in a world constantly attempting to mold you into something different represents the greatest achievement. I stand in full agreement with this statement, and I would like to explain why remaining true to yourself leads to genuine success, while pretending to be someone else ultimately brings failure.

First, let me clarify what it means to accomplish something. To accomplish means to fulfill your goals and dreams through honest means, using your genuine abilities and character. When you live according to your true self, you build a foundation that cannot be easily shaken.

I would like to illustrate this point with a story I witnessed firsthand. There was a company seeking a new director who would be well-paid and highly respected. A young woman applied for the position, but she came from modest circumstances. Despite having excellent skills and experience, she believed she needed to appear wealthy and famous to win the role.

She borrowed nearly $500,000 from various banks, rented two houses and three luxury cars to create a false image of success. When she arrived at the company, everyone believed she was wealthy and important. However, there was another candidate who had applied honestly, without pretending to be anything other than who she truly was.

After several months of evaluation, the time came for the judges to announce their decision. Both women waited nervously. Then the speaker addressed the audience with surprising news. He explained that the company had investigated both candidates and discovered that one of them had been living a fake life. He stated that such a person would likely damage the company through dishonesty and fraud.

The director position was given to the honest candidate. The woman who had lived a fake life not only failed to achieve her goal but also faced public embarrassment when her deception was revealed. Meanwhile, the woman who remained true to herself achieved her dream and experienced genuine accomplishment.

In conclusion, living authentically in a world that pressures you to become something you're not leads to real achievement. Conversely, pretending to be someone else may bring temporary satisfaction but ultimately results in disgrace when the truth emerges. Therefore, I firmly believe that being yourself is indeed the greatest accomplishment one can achieve.

The best way of work.

One question has been asked during a long time. Is it better to work alone or to work in a group?

Most of the people and analysts have got the conclusion that working in groups could be more beneficial.

A factor the support this idea it is because you get to have different thoughts, ideas and ways to see the life that can help you in bad situations. For example, if you are planning either something as big as a school event, or something as simple as a classroom presentation, there is occasions when you run out of ideas. You can count in the group. They are going to be there giving diverse solutions to the problem, otherwise, by yourself you could be struggling like if you are in road with no exit.

Working in a group sometimes can make you relax, laugh and bring positivism, even in challenging moments or when you are facing stress. Every time you have to work in this way, you do not spend boring moments. There will be always something to talk about. You and your team would be saving memories that in a future would be a moment of laugh.

Another fact about working in group is that you get to finish the work in a faster. More people working in the a series of things in a quickly way than just one, makes a big difference. It will give space to the creativity, where you can practice more, give details to the work or even do new creations.

Because you are working in a team you do not focus only in "I" you open your mind and start thinking in "we". This is going to be useful in the future, when you go out to the real world. Working with other people, you have to deal with different personalities and thoughts. The team working abilities are going to be place in your mind.

When as a team all your tasks are completed you will find a great euphoria in the results. It is going to make everyone proud of themselves and also it is going to be a method to keep pushing them up and never give up.

Sometimes when you get to work in a group it might sound or seem a difficult task. But instead, you learned new experiences and new abilities. It become a helpful tool to develop character and to grow as a person. You have to learn how to speak with the people and how to tell your ideas in a clear manner. That is why many people agreed that working in teams brings more benefits than just working alone.

Imagine waking up late on the day of an important exam, missing the school bus, and having to walk all the way to school while feeling exhausted and anxious. This is exactly what happened to me last week with my math test. Because of all that stress, I performed poorly on the exam. If I had been able to take the test online from home, I would have avoided all that trouble. Online education offers significant advantages that traditional classroom settings cannot provide. While some people argue that students might struggle with understanding material in virtual lessons, the benefits of attending classes from home clearly outweigh this concern. Students would greatly benefit from online learning because it allows them to participate in classes regardless of their location, and it gives them more time to pursue work or other activities.

Those who oppose online learning raise a valid point. They argue that students may have difficulty comprehending lessons or completing assignments when studying remotely. Without a teacher present to explain concepts directly, some learners might fall behind or struggle with their coursework.

Despite this concern, online classes offer substantial advantages that make them worthwhile. First, students can attend lessons even when they are unable to physically go to school. Whether someone is ill or visiting relatives, they can still participate in their classes from wherever they are. For instance, if I catch a cold, I wouldn't have to miss important lessons—I could simply join my class from home. Similarly, if I'm staying at a family member's house, I wouldn't have to skip school.

Additionally, online education saves valuable time that students can use for other purposes. Without the need to commute to school, high school students could work more hours at a part-time job to save money for college. They could also complete additional courses that might help their future careers or engage in hobbies they enjoy. This flexibility would allow young people to develop skills beyond their regular schoolwork while still receiving a quality education.

In conclusion, online classes provide students with the freedom to learn from anywhere, whether they are unwell or away from home. They also create opportunities to manage time more effectively, enabling students to work or pursue other interests. Rather than forcing young people to travel to school every day, we should embrace technology that makes learning more accessible and convenient for everyone.

Conserving your energy it's an important matter. But you may be wondering why? well, by conserving your energy you will be well rested, healthier and more importantly active, so you can last on your long day of work or in my case school, so I can focus on my learning in order to graduate on time.

Recently, some business companies started to conserve their body energy by working less days, but having long shifts a day. 10 hours a day to be more specific. I personally think that, this is not exactly the right way to conserve your energy and keep your body healthier. On the other hand, I would agree that you would earn more money an have better opportunities in your career despite your personal life.

Schools and government jobs etc...

If people would work 4 days a week and 10 hours a day It would totally not be good for their healthy and personal life.

First of all, If you work 10 hours a day and 4 days a week you would not have enough time to rest. As a result you would definitely be tired, exhausted and having a bad mood for not getting enough sleep. Second of all, when It comes to your personal life there would not be a family time, and no time to go out with friends therefore, I conclude that the concept of having a 10 hour shift a day would definitely not be that best way to live your life.

In terms of education, specifically talking about schools. Since I'm a student I would not be exited about attending to class for 10 hours a day. Basically because I have responsibilities outside. For example, I have to go to work, study for school and attend to my soccer training during the weekends. Also I would not be able to go work by the time school ends during weekdays and I'm sure there are students like me who have responsibilities to care of outside of school.

Now If I have to attend school for 10 hours a day and 4 days a week I can definitely say that my learning would get affected instead of improving. Nevertheless, I would not able to memorize everything I'm learning in class, because there would be a lot more topics to go over. As a human being my brain and body needs to rest, so I can keep all the information I have learned in class.

In conclusion, whether about going to school or work for 10 hours a day would not be beneficial for your professional and personal life for many reasons. For example, It could affect your health and your emotions which could lead you to be stressed out or having a bad mood not to mention that It could also affect your personal life by not having the necessary time to take care of your responsibilities outside of work.

The answer is simple: by preserving your energy levels, you can stay well-rested, maintain better health, and remain more productive throughout your day—whether at work or, in my case, at school. This allows me to concentrate on my studies and achieve my academic goals on schedule.

While it is true that workers might earn more money and have better career advancement opportunities, the cost to their personal lives can be significant.

The same applies to schools and government positions. If people were required to work ten hours daily for four days instead, this would likely have negative consequences for both their health and their personal lives.

First and foremost, working ten hours each day would leave insufficient time for proper rest. Consequently, employees would likely feel fatigued, exhausted, and irritable due to lack of adequate sleep. Secondly, their personal lives would suffer considerably. There would be less time available for family activities and social interactions with friends. Therefore, I believe that the ten-hour workday model is not the optimal way to live one's life.

For instance, I need to work, study for my courses, and attend soccer practice on weekends. Furthermore, I would be unable to work after school during the week, and I am certain many students face similar external responsibilities.

If I were required to attend school for ten hours each day across four days, my learning would undoubtedly be negatively affected rather than improved. I would struggle to retain all the information presented in class because there would be an overwhelming number of topics to cover. As human beings, both our minds and bodies require rest in order to process and maintain what we have learned.

In conclusion, attending school or working for ten hours daily would not be advantageous for one's professional and personal life for several important reasons. It could impact both physical health and emotional wellbeing, potentially causing stress and mood problems. Additionally, it could harm personal life by eliminating the necessary time to handle responsibilities outside of work or school.
