Is it better to work in groups? Does collaborative work help you concentrate? Is it easier and more enjoyable to complete tasks with others? These are common questions that people ask. While some prefer working alone, I believe that group work offers greater advantages for several important reasons, including the opportunity to share ideas, finish tasks promptly, and enjoy the experience while meeting new people.

One significant benefit of working in groups is the ability to share and combine ideas. When people work together, they bring different perspectives and thoughts to the table. This collaboration allows for brainstorming sessions where everyone contributes their opinions about a project or assignment. Through discussion, group members can ensure that everyone understands the topic clearly. This is particularly valuable because each person brings something unique to the group, making the work more comprehensive and well-rounded.

Another advantage is that group work helps tasks get completed efficiently and on schedule. Working alone can sometimes be challenging because it takes longer to finish, deadlines may be missed, and assistance might not be available when needed. In contrast, groups typically consist of three or four members, which makes the workflow much faster. By dividing responsibilities and assigning specific roles to each person, the group can work more effectively. This division of labor ensures that everyone contributes and the project progresses smoothly toward completion.

Furthermore, group work is often more enjoyable and provides opportunities to interact with people we might not normally communicate with. Many students prefer working alone because they feel uncomfortable approaching strangers. However, I find that collaborating with others can be both fun and rewarding. Working in a group creates a more relaxed atmosphere where people can share jokes and laughter. Although this might occasionally cause minor distractions, it also brings joy and positivity to the workplace. This friendly environment makes the work feel less stressful and more satisfying.

In conclusion, working in groups is more beneficial than working individually. Through collaboration, people can share ideas, meet deadlines more easily, and enjoy the process of working together. Groups allow members to discuss and confirm that everyone comprehends the task before beginning. Learning to work as a team teaches us to encourage one another, support our colleagues, and stay determined. Demonstrating teamwork, hard work, and commitment leads to greater success in any group project.

In today's society, people constantly pressure others to conform and follow the latest trends. Whether it is wearing the same hairstyles, dyeing hair in popular colors, or trying to achieve a certain body type, many individuals fear standing out from the crowd. This is precisely why I agree with Emerson's statement about the importance of being yourself. When you embrace your true identity, you become unique, follow your own dreams, and develop genuine confidence.

Rather than imitating others, imagine the freedom that comes with being different. You could play sports that genuinely interest you, regardless of whether they are popular. You might develop your own fashion sense and create unique clothing combinations that reflect your personality. Most importantly, you would be able to express your creativity without worrying about following whatever is currently in style. Your authentic self becomes your greatest asset.

Regarding dreams, everyone has aspirations, though they may differ from person to person. Perhaps you dream of becoming a doctor, while someone else aspires to be a musician. When you truly discover who you are, you will have the courage to pursue your own dreams rather than someone else's expectations. This path leads to genuine happiness because you will be doing what you love. Each day becomes enjoyable, and even difficult moments will seem more manageable. You will naturally find positivity in various situations because you appreciate both who you are and what you do.

Confidence is another significant benefit of being true to yourself. Unfortunately, many people struggle with self-assurance in contemporary times. However, when you are confident, the opinions of others lose their power over you. You stop worrying about criticism and instead concentrate on your personal goals. You trust your own judgments and believe in your abilities, regardless of what challenges arise. Furthermore, your self-assurance can inspire others who may be struggling to find their own identity. You become a positive example for those who have not yet discovered their true selves.

Ultimately, being yourself means ignoring external pressures and living according to your own principles. Life offers only one opportunity, so it should be lived authentically. Establish your own objectives and resist the temptation to imitate others. If you continuously try to be someone else, you will never experience true satisfaction, and you will miss the chance to achieve your deepest desires. Embrace your individual light within you and let it shine. Try being yourself, for it is the most rewarding journey you will ever undertake.

Many employers are looking for candidates who are responsible, hardworking, and have previous experience in the field. While I understand that experience is often valued, I believe I should still be considered for the position because I am a responsible and dedicated worker, even though I may not have direct experience in this particular type of work.

First and foremost, I am committed to working hard to succeed in this role. I am willing to put in the effort to learn and understand the responsibilities that come with the job. It may take some time to become fully proficient, but I am confident that my dedication will make it worthwhile. I am not someone who avoids work; rather, I am a quick learner who adapts well to new situations. I have held other positions in the past, and I performed well in those roles because I genuinely wanted to succeed and contribute to the team. My motivation comes from a sincere desire to be part of the organization and to grow within it.

Unfortunately, some employers are reluctant to hire candidates without specific experience. They may turn away qualified individuals or dismiss them as not worth the time investment. This reality can be challenging for job seekers who are eager to prove themselves. In today's world, many people accept positions simply because they need the income to cover rent and other expenses, rather than because they are truly passionate about the work. They may not consider the long-term implications of working long hours for low pay. Conversely, some individuals seek jobs that offer better compensation and shorter working hours. What I am trying to convey is that I would appreciate the opportunity to be hired for this position, as I am determined to work hard and eventually advance to a management role. I believe I am qualified for this opportunity, even without prior experience. Willingness to work hard and learn is a quality that life teaches us, and it could benefit both myself and the company in the future. If I work hard enough, I could enjoy a better quality of life and be prepared to handle various tasks that the job may require. I am ready to face whatever challenges come my way.

However, I acknowledge that it may take time to perform at my best. Adapting to a new type of work can be difficult because people become accustomed to their previous routines. Adjusting to a different environment does not happen overnight, and it requires patience and perseverance. I am prepared to make that adjustment and work diligently to reach a management position. Some may believe that adapting to a new job is easy and happens quickly, but this is not always true. Transitioning from one type of work to another can be challenging. Additionally, some individuals can be unsupportive and may try to make new employees feel unwelcome, hoping they will quit. This behavior is unfair, and if I encounter such treatment, I will not simply accept it. I want to perform my duties peacefully and without unnecessary interference.

It is natural for people to aspire to better positions, even when they are just starting out. Seeking advancement is a normal part of professional growth, and I am no exception. However, some colleagues may not allow you to progress peacefully and may attempt to undermine your efforts. If you remain resilient and do not let their negativity affect you, they will eventually tire of their behavior and recognize your improvement. I would appreciate the opportunity to prove myself to those who may doubt my abilities. I am determined not to be a complacent employee; instead, I will work diligently to achieve a management role and eventually establish my own business. Many people dream of becoming business owners, and I am no different. However, achieving this dream requires hard work and dedication, which I am prepared to provide.

In conclusion, even without direct experience in a particular field, a candidate can still be excellent if they possess the right attitude and work ethic. Such individuals are capable of achieving great things and may even become successful entrepreneurs. Success requires consistent effort and determination, regardless of whether it takes one year or three. I am willing to put in the necessary work to achieve my goals. I am ready to take the risk and excel in this role, potentially surpassing others who have more experience. Learning new skills and gaining knowledge from different types of work makes a person more versatile and qualified. Having a broad understanding of various roles can open doors to new opportunities and even business ownership. I am prepared to work hard and take that risk.

Many people believe that having a positive mindset is not essential for achieving success in life, but I completely disagree with this viewpoint. In today's fast-paced world, maintaining a good attitude toward others has become more important than ever.

One significant reason why a positive attitude matters is that it can help you land your dream job. When you approach people with optimism and enthusiasm, they are more likely to notice you and consider you for opportunities. Employers often prefer hiring individuals who demonstrate a positive outlook because they can contribute to a better work environment. A positive person may be offered a position or a chance to advance their career simply because they made a good impression through their optimistic approach.

Another important benefit is that a positive attitude can brighten someone else's day. Imagine meeting someone who is having a difficult day; your cheerful demeanor and friendly words could completely change their mood. This creates a chain reaction, as that person might then spread their improved mood to others, making the world a slightly better place.

Finally, having a positive attitude greatly improves communication and relationships. People are naturally drawn to those who are optimistic and kind. This makes it easier to connect with others, build strong friendships, and develop valuable professional networks.

In summary, I firmly believe that a positive attitude is indeed the key to success in life.

I believe that I also know that you can accomplish other things by doing something different, but I chose to help myself and others. Also, I understand that you can accomplish something by doing nothing. But one of them is being aware of problems. By doing all of this, I consider myself accomplishing many things.

Staying busy is essential if we want to achieve our goals in life. In my view, people who remain active accomplish far more than those who prefer to do nothing. When we constantly engage in productive activities, our minds stay sharp and we feel meaningful. For instance, attending school, maintaining employment, and assisting others are all ways to stay productive. Once we develop the habit of doing things consistently, we naturally want to continue achieving. Additionally, there are certain situations where not taking action actually creates problems. As Thomas Jefferson wisely stated, "never to be idle," which encourages us to avoid becoming the kind of people who waste their time doing nothing.

To begin with, education plays a vital role in personal growth. When we attend school regularly, our minds remain active and focused. I can personally relate to this because my daily routine involves waking up early, attending classes, completing homework, and staying engaged with my studies. This constant involvement makes me feel productive and accomplished. Furthermore, when I encounter difficulties in my schoolwork, I seek assistance from my teachers, and when my classmates need support, I gladly share my knowledge. Keeping our minds occupied with learning helps us develop better communication skills and improves our overall well-being.

Additionally, having a job provides valuable experience for future success. My first job taught me essential computer skills, which initially seemed impossible to learn but eventually became beneficial for my education. This experience showed me that achieving goals requires genuine interest and effort. Without motivation, we cannot accomplish anything meaningful. In my second job, I learned how to use mobile devices to take customer orders by dedicating myself to learning. Now, in my current position, I have developed numerous skills including answering telephone calls, processing orders, and delivering excellent customer service.

Furthermore, helping others represents another important way to achieve fulfillment. When we assist those in need, such as homeless individuals, we gain the opportunity to understand their circumstances and empathize with their struggles. Some people choose to leave their homes due to disagreements with family rules, but this is rarely the best solution since everyone needs support from others. Listening to elders who possess greater life experience is also crucial for achieving success. I speak from personal experience because there was a time when my parents left me responsible for my two younger brothers, and we had no food or shelter. Witnessing people in need now reminds me of that difficult period in my life.

In conclusion, I strongly believe that accomplishing more comes from remaining active and engaged in meaningful activities. Through education, employment, and helping others, we can achieve numerous things and develop as individuals. While there may be rare situations where inactivity leads to problems, the best approach to success is through consistent effort and productivity. By staying busy with positive activities, I consider myself to be continuously achieving my goals.

Have you ever wondered whether attending classes from home can actually help you? Many students aspire to receive a good education and achieve success, but various challenges often make traditional public or private schools unsuitable for them. As a result, some choose online education, and many have reported significant benefits. These students often explain that when they were struggling in conventional schools, switching to online learning transformed their academic experience and overall well-being.

While some people hold a different view, my perspective comes from personal family experiences, stories I've heard on podcasts, and accounts from public figures.

One of my relatives, let's call her Sarah, faced considerable difficulties that made attending regular school impossible. She struggled to maintain her grades while also dealing with the challenges of getting to school on time. Sarah was battling an eating disorder, which made managing both her health and school responsibilities extremely overwhelming. Her family decided to enroll her in online school, and this choice made a tremendous difference. She could complete her assignments from home while attending doctor appointments and focusing on her recovery. Additionally, some teachers visited her house to help with schoolwork. Through online education, Sarah managed to overcome her eating disorder and achieved remarkable success. After several years of continued study, she eventually became a lawyer. It's quite remarkable how someone facing such significant challenges could accomplish so much.

Some people might find it difficult to understand how she achieved this through online school. They might think it's unfair or that home schooling cannot truly help someone become successful. However, when you hear so many stories about positive experiences with online education, you have to acknowledge that it works for some individuals, even if not everyone.

Many radio podcasts have discussed real-life situations related to this topic. One story that particularly stood out to me involved a mother talking about her son, who was very popular on social media. She explained that throughout his high school years, other students bullied him and tried to start fights with him for no apparent reason. The mother decided to enroll her son in online schooling. He attended virtual classes and had video conferences with his teachers regularly. He found this arrangement much easier and explained that he could concentrate better because there were no distractions or other students trying to bother him. Since managing social media was important to him, he could balance both his online presence and his education simultaneously. Some might argue that he should learn to face difficult people and not always avoid them. While this has some truth, sometimes when someone has experienced too much negativity, choosing a different path might be the best decision.

Public figures have also spoken in interviews about choosing home schooling and how helpful it was for them. One social media personality explained that being well-known online comes with many difficulties. She mentioned dealing with harsh criticism, constant exposure, and having her name always discussed by others. She was bullied numerous times, and it became increasingly difficult to cope with. At one point, she developed depression and found it impossible to continue attending regular school. Her teachers suggested online schooling. She followed this advice and completed both her high school and college education through distance learning. She mentioned feeling much more successful as a result. She stated that online school was the best decision she ever made, and for college, she chose to attend a public university while continuing her social media career. Some critics fail to see how this benefited her. However, the transformation was significant - she no longer fears what people think of her online. Sometimes people need distance from traditional school settings, and when they feel ready, they can return to regular education.

The importance of sharing these experiences is that others facing similar struggles can learn from them. People dealing with comparable challenges can read about past experiences and determine whether online schooling might work for them. In the future, others can look back at these stories to understand what people went through and how much they were struggling. This helps provide perspective on how things were in the past compared to now. One solution for those finding traditional school difficult is to consider online education for various reasons. Additionally, it's important to recognize that individuals who are prominent on social media often struggle to cope with the negativity they receive. A solution for society is for people to stop spreading hate toward others.

Modern technology enables individuals to accomplish numerous activities without any direct interaction with others. People can borrow books, shop online, and play games without speaking to anyone. Nevertheless, technology has both beneficial and harmful impacts on our lives. While some argue that technology is advantageous because everyone can use it during emergencies, many others believe that technology alters people's behavior and that individuals now prioritize what happens behind a screen over real-life relationships.

Some people argue that technology is positive because it can be used in emergency situations. Imagine a family living far from any neighbors who needs assistance. In such circumstances, technology becomes essential. For instance, when I was in my home country, many families resided in remote areas away from the city. Some of them lacked any means of communication with relatives or other people. Unfortunately, several of these families experienced serious difficulties because when someone became ill, they could not receive help from others, and some even passed away due to the lack of technological devices at that critical moment.

Furthermore, many people consider technology harmful because it can change how people behave. In the past, people were more respectful toward one another, even without formal education. However, critics argue that individuals' attitudes have changed due to exposure to movies, music, novels, and cartoons. It is also true that people who use technology constantly may develop mental health issues or damage their vision from excessive screen time. For example, I know a family with a fifteen-year-old daughter who enjoys watching numerous television programs. This teenager behaves as if she is older than other young people her age and refuses to obey her parents. Her behavior is problematic, yet this reflects how her parents are raising her. She goes out whenever she wishes with whoever she wants. Sometimes I believe this is her parents' fault because they keep purchasing various technological devices for her. They do not pay attention to how their daughter uses technology. In contrast, allowing children to use technology at a young age can be detrimental because some of them do not use it appropriately. When they grow older, their parents cannot control them because they have already learned negative behaviors from technology. Instead, parents should spend time outdoors with their children rather than letting them use devices.

Additionally, many people believe that technology is negative because individuals now value what occurs on screens more than the people physically around them. It is accurate that many people concentrate on screens almost constantly. Psychologists have stated that face-to-face conversations are more effective because people can communicate more clearly about situations. They are correct because technology allows individuals to deceive others while hiding behind their screens. Currently, companies produce more devices that cause people to become increasingly absorbed in technology. Furthermore, approximately ninety percent of people pay more attention to technology than to their families or those nearby. There are many examples of deception through technology. About five months ago, I read a book titled "Behind the Web" that fascinated me. The main character was a female teacher who was communicating with someone she knew nothing about. While exchanging messages, the person behind the screen pretended to be a man but was actually a girl disguised as a male. When the teacher suggested a video call, the person refused because she was lying. Many similar situations occur in real life.

In conclusion, technology can be either beneficial or harmful, depending on how individuals choose to use it. Technology continues to advance, but people must learn when and how to use it appropriately. Technology has the power to significantly transform many people's lives.

Do you believe imagination holds more value than knowledge? In my opinion, imagination is far more significant because it allows us to visualize countless possibilities. Unlike knowledge, which requires studying and understanding facts, imagination lets us envision success and happiness in our lives. My imagination had become reality. That experience taught me that believing in your dreams and visualizing success can actually help you achieve it. Through this, I became one of the best players in middle school, and now I look forward to becoming famous someday.

In summary, imagination matters more than knowledge because it enables us to see our future before it actually happens. When we imagine something strongly enough, we can make it come true.

I agree with Ralph Waldo Emerson because staying in one's comfort zone limits personal growth. It is essential to step beyond what we already know and discover new possibilities. Without exploration, we can never understand our true potential or develop as individuals. While it is acceptable to feel content at times, emergencies and opportunities often require us to venture into unfamiliar territory. In many communities, people become too comfortable with their current situations and fail to pursue greater achievements.

I believe that continuous exploration leads to significant personal development. For instance, if Bill Gates had been satisfied with his initial accomplishments and never explored new possibilities, he would never have founded Microsoft or become successful. Similarly, if Barack Obama had been content with his existing education and never pursued further opportunities, he would never have become a senator or the first African American president of the United States. Without pushing beyond our limits, we can never discover what we are truly capable of achieving.

Exploring beyond our mastered skills often reveals hidden talents and unexpected growth. We cannot discover our worth or abilities without attempting new challenges. Some individuals believe they will fail if they try something different, but this mindset prevents them from advancing. The more willing we are to explore, the further we can go in life. We should always strive to reach new levels rather than remain satisfied with what we have already achieved.

My mother always advises me to never be completely satisfied with my current position and to step out of my comfort zone. This advice helps us understand our true capabilities. For example, if your supervisor leaves and management is seeking a replacement, but you choose to stay in your current role because you are afraid of taking on new responsibilities, you may never know what you could have accomplished. Similarly, some college students with a master's degree are afraid to pursue a doctorate because they believe their current achievement is their limit.

Being happy with our current situation is not necessarily negative, but we should always strive for improvement. We should fight for a better future and never become stagnant. As Neil Armstrong famously said, it is sometimes necessary to take a giant leap. Many people need to take that leap in their own lives. The more we explore, the more we learn about ourselves and the possibilities that await us.

Many educational institutions now provide remote learning opportunities, allowing students to participate in lessons from home through internet platforms or video calls. This approach offers significant advantages for learners who struggle with social interactions or find it difficult to communicate with their peers and teachers. Additionally, it supports those who have encountered negative situations at traditional school environments. When students can study in surroundings where they feel at ease, they tend to concentrate better and face fewer distractions.

Some critics suggest that studying from home may not be beneficial for students. They argue that learners might become easily distracted and fail to complete their assignments. Others believe that students may struggle to teach themselves without direct supervision. Furthermore, opponents point out that remote learning prevents students from experiencing traditional school life and developing important social skills.

However, these concerns do not outweigh the benefits for certain students. Every learner has a unique background, and some have faced challenging circumstances that affect how they behave in group settings. By offering them the option to study remotely, we give them the opportunity to demonstrate their true abilities. Forcing such students to interact constantly with others in a conventional classroom setting can actually prevent them from reaching their full potential, as they become distracted by social pressures.

Remote learning is particularly valuable for students who have experienced bullying or other traumatic events at school. These negative experiences can seriously impact their motivation to attend classes and their overall academic success. Bullying remains a significant issue in education today, affecting many learners' wellbeing and performance. Online classes can protect these students from further harm and allow them to focus entirely on their studies in a safe environment.

Comfort and a sense of security play crucial roles in effective learning. When students study in familiar surroundings, they often achieve better results because they feel relaxed and can concentrate without external干扰. A supportive family environment can also motivate learners to persist through challenges and work toward their goals.

In conclusion, educational institutions should definitely offer distance learning as a valid option. This approach helps students who find social interactions difficult, supports those who have experienced negative situations at school, and enables learners who perform better in comfortable environments to reach their full potential. Providing this choice could significantly increase the number of students who succeed academically.

The question of whether students would benefit from attending classes remotely from home is worth examining carefully. I firmly believe that learning from home offers no real advantages, and I would like to explain three main reasons for this position.

First and foremost, when students take online classes from home, they often fail to absorb any meaningful knowledge by the end of the course. Unlike in a traditional classroom setting where the teacher can monitor their engagement, at home students tend to rush through assignments simply to complete them quickly and move on to other activities. As a result, they show little genuine interest in the material. When the time comes to demonstrate what they have learned, they find themselves completely unprepared. In my own experience, studying in front of a computer screen creates a mental block that makes it difficult to retain information effectively.

Second, the home environment presents countless distractions that easily divert students' attention away from their studies. When learning remotely, students have immediate access to various electronic devices such as smartphones, the very computer they are using for class, or the television. Family responsibilities can also interfere significantly. For instance, when family members see that a student is at home, they may ask them to look after younger siblings or help with household chores. While friends can be distracting in a classroom, this problem becomes even worse at home because younger students often have friends visiting to play video games, which pulls their focus away from their lessons entirely.

Finally, traditional classroom learning provides a more effective way of acquiring knowledge through direct interaction with teachers. I personally value the opportunity to engage with both my instructor and classmates about the subject matter we are studying. This dialogue helps me develop a better understanding of the content and exposes me to different perspectives. Watching a teacher deliver a lesson in person allows students to absorb information far more efficiently than watching a screen. Furthermore, material learned on a computer tends to be forgotten almost immediately, whereas face-to-face instruction creates lasting impressions.

In conclusion, attending classes in a physical classroom and interacting directly with teachers and peers represents the optimal approach to learning. By taking courses remotely from home, students risk wasting an entire semester because they will be unable to achieve the grades needed to pass. The availability of electronic distractions at home makes it far too easy for students to lose focus. Traditional classroom attendance provides not only educational benefits but also teaches important social skills that are essential for success in the wider world beyond school.

I believe that individuals should start making their own decisions because this allows them to learn about life, develop a better understanding of how the world works, and learn to value themselves while becoming more capable and independent.

There will be moments when you stumble or face situations you never expected, and this is when you truly realize how difficult life can sometimes be. Additionally, mistakes are completely natural. No one is perfect, and life can catch you off guard when you least expect it. You must be prepared to face whatever comes your way, whether it seems easy or challenging. When you make your own choices, you become better at making the right decisions for yourself.

As we get older, life either makes us stronger or weaker, and this is entirely up to us. The best approach is to understand that anything can happen without warning. It will occur at the right time or perhaps not at the ideal moment you were hoping for. Whatever causes you pain will ultimately make you stronger, and this is how you know you are truly living.

A city curfew for teenagers is a reasonable measure that should be supported. If young people are prohibited from being on the streets after midnight, they will be following municipal regulations, which ultimately benefits everyone involved.

In conclusion, replacing students' favorite foods with healthier options would be a bad decision for the school to make.

I disagree with the school board's proposal to add an extra hour and a half to the school day each day. This change would lead to more homework and class assignments for students. It would also create additional conflicts in their daily lives. Furthermore, students would struggle to stay focused during those additional hours in the classroom.

Many students would also find it challenging to manage their homework alongside other responsibilities. For example, after finishing a long day of classes, students would need to spend even more time studying, leaving them with little time to rest or relax. This increased burden would likely cause stress and frustration among students.

In addition, extending the school day would result in more conflicts and drama among students. With extra time spent at school, students would have more opportunities to engage in disagreements and problems. This could distract them from their studies and negatively impact their academic performance. As a result, their grades might suffer because they would be more focused on conflicts rather than learning. The additional time at school would not necessarily lead to better educational outcomes.

Finally, students have many other commitments outside of school that would be affected by a longer school day. Many students participate in sports, spend time with their families, or enjoy hobbies after school. An extended school day would cut into these important activities. For instance, students might miss family dinners, recreational activities, or time spent with friends. These experiences are valuable for their overall development and well-being. Students should have the opportunity to balance their education with other aspects of their lives.

In conclusion, adding an extra hour and a half to the school day would not be beneficial for students. It would increase their workload, create more opportunities for conflict, and take away time they need for other important activities. The school board should reconsider this plan and explore other ways to improve education without placing additional burden on students.

Consider a world filled with darkness, sadness, and hopelessness. This is what could happen if people believe that tiny gestures of goodwill cannot make any difference. However, performing small acts of kindness can actually transform both individuals and the entire world.

One significant benefit of being kind is that it helps build a positive reputation. There are many ways to develop a good reputation, but one of the simplest methods is showing kindness to those around you. This approach can strengthen all types of relationships. Additionally, when you are nice to others, they often respond with kindness in return, which can have a powerful effect on everyone involved. I have personally experienced this many times. For instance, when I offer someone a genuine compliment, I often see their face light up with happiness. Similarly, on days when I feel unhappy and others notice, they tend to be more considerate toward me. Being known as a caring person makes you more memorable in any setting. People begin to recognize you as someone who brings positivity, and they may even seek out your company or return your kindness.

Another important way kindness can help is by improving our communities and potentially the whole world. Unfortunately, our society has many problems, but we can work toward fixing them through simple acts of generosity. When you treat someone kindly, they feel pleased and are more likely to pass that positivity on to others. This creates a chain reaction where one act of kindness inspires another, and then another. The more people who choose to be kind, the more others they will influence to do the same. I witnessed this happen at my school. After I decided to be more caring toward my classmates, I became more popular. Eventually, other students started behaving more nicely to gain similar recognition. Everyone benefits when kindness spreads in this way.

Finally, one of the most meaningful ways to impact others is by helping them feel better about themselves. As the famous storyteller Aesop once noted, no act of kindness, no matter how small, is ever wasted. Giving someone a compliment can completely brighten their day. This not only affects that person but also influences those who witness the interaction, as they recognize something beautiful happening. Kindness has the power to change lives. I can personally attest to this. Around the age of eleven, I faced difficulties both at school and at home. However, the friends who showed me kindness made that year truly special, and some of them remain my closest companions today. By offering support to someone who truly needs it, such as someone struggling with personal problems, you can help them develop a more positive and joyful outlook on life.

These examples demonstrate that regardless of how minor an act of kindness may seem, it has the potential to profoundly transform someone's existence.

It offers convenience for those who lack time to visit stores, allowing them to purchase items like clothing or groceries online from home. Additionally, technology gives us the ability to create things that humans could not accomplish before.

However, technology also has negative effects. Have you observed young children playing with toys as they did in the past? Now we see five to ten-year-olds owning phones or gaming consoles. Both children and young adults can become addicted to these devices. As a result, some people may experience vision problems from excessive use. Nevertheless, technology itself is not to blame; it is our own responsibility to take care of our health.

Technology influences our lives by decreasing face-to-face interactions, but simultaneously it provides numerous benefits for our current generation and those to come.

Some educational institutions now provide students with the opportunity to participate in lessons remotely through online platforms or video conferencing. This approach is intended to assist learners who are unable to attend physical classrooms due to health conditions or other circumstances. While distance learning and traditional schooling share certain advantages, they are not equally effective for everyone.

In my view, studying from home can be helpful for certain students, particularly those facing health challenges, but it is not ideal for learners who simply wish to avoid school, as they may struggle to acquire knowledge effectively.

First, distance education offers clear advantages for students with medical conditions that prevent them from traveling to school. For instance, students with mobility issues or chronic illnesses like arthritis may find it extremely difficult to attend classes in person. In such cases, online lessons or video calls with teachers can serve as a practical alternative. These students can still receive instruction and eventually earn qualifications that will support their future prospects. Additionally, learners who have experienced difficulties at school, such as conflicts with peers, may also benefit from studying at home. This arrangement allows them to continue their education in a safer environment while receiving appropriate support.

However, I believe this approach is not suitable for students who simply do not want to attend school. When learners lack motivation and have no teacher directly guiding them, they may become distracted and fail to engage meaningfully with the material. Without proper supervision, they are unlikely to develop a thorough understanding of the subject matter.

Furthermore, students who need to immerse themselves in a language may also struggle with home-based learning. For example, non-native speakers trying to master English would benefit far more from being in a school setting where they hear the language constantly throughout the day. At home, they might have limited exposure, which would slow their progress significantly. Schools provide valuable opportunities for interaction with both teachers and peers, which accelerates language acquisition.

In conclusion, distance learning is not universally advantageous. It works well for some students, particularly those with health issues or those who have faced problems in traditional school settings. Nevertheless, it can be challenging for learners who lack self-discipline or who need intensive language exposure. Ultimately, whether studying at home or in a classroom, the most important factor is the student's commitment to learning and their determination to succeed in life.

On the contrary, a person who treats others rudely and shows disrespect likely did not receive adequate moral education at home. Therefore, our attitude serves as a reflection of how we were raised.

Additionally, a positive attitude can greatly benefit our academic pursuits. Teachers are more willing to help students who show enthusiasm and eagerness to learn. When a student demonstrates a good attitude during lessons, it shows the teacher that they genuinely care about their education and are motivated to succeed.

However, I disagree with this view because we can learn to manage our emotions and develop a more positive outlook on life.

In conclusion, maintaining a positive attitude can help us achieve our goals because it reflects our personality, our upbringing, and our willingness to interact well with others. A good attitude demonstrates how we were raised and how much we value learning and personal growth.

As time goes by, technology continues to develop at a rapid pace. This advancement is causing people to communicate with each other less frequently, and it is also negatively affecting our education system.

The more technology advances, the worse personal communication becomes. Many people prefer to shop and handle their errands online rather than going out into the real world. This is problematic because fewer people will have jobs when everyone simply orders everything from their computers instead of visiting stores.

Additionally, students are struggling to concentrate in school because of technology. By the time children reach sixth grade, most of them already own smartphones. These devices distract them from their lessons, and teachers find it increasingly difficult to keep their attention. Many young people today spend hours ordering products over the internet, often purchasing items that are not appropriate for their age. In a way, technology is taking over our world.

In conclusion, as technology continues to advance, we are seeing a decline in face-to-face interactions and a deterioration in the quality of education. It is important to find a balance between using technology and maintaining meaningful human connections.

This essay will discuss a proposal that some institutions are considering, which involves switching to a four-day school week while adding two extra hours to each school day. I will share my opinion on whether my high school should adopt this approach, examining both the advantages and disadvantages, as well as suggesting steps that should be taken before any implementation.

Imagine receiving a letter from your school announcing plans to have students attend only four days per week, with two additional hours added to the daily schedule. I disagree with this proposal because it would negatively impact my high school rather than benefit it. The first major concern is the effect on after-school programs and activities. If two hours are added to each day, the school day would total approximately ten hours, leaving students exhausted and far less likely to participate in extracurricular activities. Consequently, the school might need to cancel these programs entirely. This would be particularly damaging at the high school level, where many juniors and seniors have part-time jobs and would struggle to maintain their work schedules.

Implementing this proposal would bring both advantages and disadvantages. On the positive side, extending the school day would provide more time for classroom instruction and homework completion. Additionally, the school could potentially conserve energy and resources by operating on fewer days. However, the drawbacks are significant. After-school programs would likely suffer from reduced participation, and some students might be forced to adjust their working hours or even leave their jobs entirely, which could create financial difficulties for many families.

Before implementing such a change, schools should take several important steps. First, administrators should hold an internal meeting to thoroughly discuss the proposal. Second, a separate meeting should be organized with parents to explain the details of the plan. Third, a written explanation should be sent home for parents to review and sign, indicating whether they support or oppose the implementation. Only after completing these steps should the school make a final decision.

In conclusion, I disagree with implementing this idea at my school because it would cause more harm than good. The disadvantages are substantial, including the potential loss of after-school activities, job conflicts for working students, and increased fatigue. The current schedule at my school works well because students can participate in sports, join clubs, and maintain part-time employment. I believe my school should keep its existing schedule, as adding two hours to each day would create more problems than solutions.

I can see why some people believe extending the school day by ninety minutes would give children more opportunities to learn.

However, I believe this is not a good idea, and here's why. First of all, many students participate in activities after school, such as sports, community service, and helping around the house. These activities are important to young people, and adding more time to the school day would mean they couldn't take part in these valuable activities. Additionally, students need time to complete their homework and study for tests. If they spend extra hours at school, they won't have adequate time to review their schoolwork or prepare for the next day's lessons.

Another significant concern is family time. Many families look forward to spending evenings together, whether it's having dinner at a restaurant, going for walks, or simply relaxing at home. Extending the school day would take away this precious time that families need to bond and connect with each other. Parents might also struggle with transportation and scheduling if their children finish school later.

Some parents have suggested that if the school day is going to be longer, students should be allowed to arrive later in the morning so they can get more sleep. Getting enough rest is crucial for academic performance, and tired students struggle to concentrate and learn effectively.

Weekend time would also be affected. Many families enjoy weekend trips and outings together. With additional homework and projects from a longer school day, students would have less time to enjoy these family activities.

There's also a practical concern for schools themselves. If students have to spend more time at school, some families might decide to transfer their children to schools with shorter days or even consider homeschooling. This could lead to declining enrollment, which might eventually force schools to close. Such outcomes would negatively affect teachers too, as they could lose their jobs and face difficulties finding new employment.

In conclusion, while the intention behind adding time to the school day may be positive, the potential problems it would create for students, families, and schools make it impractical.

His supportive words helped me believe in myself, and consequently, my performance gradually improved.

Based on the reasoning and examples presented above, I maintain that true self-esteem originates from praise because it provides determination and helps individuals build confidence. Therefore, I encourage all educators to recognize their students' efforts and make them feel capable of achieving more.

Dear Principal,

I believe that changing the grade requirement to a B average is a positive step. Many students currently have only a C average, and if they participate in sports, their academic performance could decline even further. Students need to prioritize their education over extracurricular activities. Without this policy, some students may end up failing their classes.

If the requirement remains at a B average, students will be motivated to work harder academically. When students receive their progress reports and see low grades, they will understand that they have been dedicating too much time to sports rather than studying. This feedback helps them recognize where they need to improve.

I recommend that the principal first test how students respond to this change. If it proves effective, the policy should remain in place. However, there should be room for flexibility if needed.

Some students may complain about having to study more, but this requirement ultimately benefits them. Additionally, the school's reputation could improve. Instead of being known for allowing students with a C average to participate in sports, the school could become recognized for having students who maintain a B average or higher. This would be a significant improvement.

It is important for students to maintain good grades because those who fail to do so may not pass to the next grade level. This new policy will be challenging, but students who genuinely enjoy sports and school activities will put in the necessary effort to meet the requirements. However, if a student genuinely tries their best—attending tutoring, completing all assignments, and turning in their work on time—then teachers should consider allowing them to participate.

I believe everyone is capable of achieving at least a B average. We are all intelligent in our own ways. This policy will work well, but only if students stop complaining and actually put in the effort. If they continue to be lazy, sleep in class, and not try their best, their grades will not improve, and that will be their own responsibility.

We want our school to be recognized for having student athletes with strong academics. Those who want to succeed will keep trying until they achieve their goals. However, if a student simply does not care about their education, that is their personal choice.

I fully support this policy. As I have mentioned, every student is capable of succeeding academically, even if they do not believe it themselves.

Trying your best in school does not have to be a negative experience. Even if students only put in effort to play sports, the outcome is positive. A student who was previously failing can now say they are passing all their classes. They should not worry about what others think—they should do this for themselves.

This essay examines the advantages and disadvantages of implementing a four-day school week, where each school day would be ten hours long. Some people believe this approach would help conserve energy and resources, but I have serious concerns about whether this model would actually work for students and teachers.

As a student, I can see some potential benefits, but I strongly disagree with extending the school day by two hours. Currently, many students spend eight hours in school, which is already quite exhausting. Spending the entire day sitting in classrooms can be mentally and physically draining. For instance, in almost every class, there are students who fall asleep because they are overwhelmed with homework, have part-time jobs after school, or participate in sports. If students are already this tired, imagine how much worse it would be to add two more hours to their school day. While a three-day weekend might sound appealing, the reality is that the extended hours would negate any potential benefits.

The argument that this schedule saves energy is also flawed. Adding two extra hours to Monday through Thursday still amounts to eight hours of energy use, which is exactly what would be spent on the fifth day of a traditional week. Therefore, this approach does not actually result in energy savings. The math simply does not support this claim.

There are also practical concerns for students with busy schedules. One student I know supports the four-day week because it would give him more time to complete homework and spend time with his girlfriend. However, my classmate who plays basketball has a different perspective. After school, he trains for two hours and then works for four hours to help his parents with expenses. By the time he gets home, he still needs to complete his homework. Adding more hours to the school day would make his situation even more difficult. Many students are in similar positions, helping their families while trying to keep up with their studies.

Teachers would also struggle with ten-hour teaching days. They are not machines programmed by the government to work endlessly. After a full day of teaching, they would be just as exhausted as students, and they may not support this new schedule either.

My school should not adopt this model without carefully considering the needs of everyone involved, including students, teachers, and administrative staff. A fair decision must take into account how this change would affect the entire school community. Additionally, we have no guarantee that this system would work well in an educational setting. While some businesses have implemented four-day workweeks successfully, schools are different environments. Students participate in various activities such as sports, clubs, and part-time jobs that differ from typical workplace responsibilities. What works for a company may not necessarily work for a high school.

In conclusion, a four-day school week with longer daily hours is not the best solution for our educational environment.

Mobile phones have become extremely popular among American teenagers, who frequently use them to text and call their friends. However, this habit is beginning to create problems in schools across the United States. Students are using their phones during class time and even at lunch, which leads to teachers confiscating devices and taking them to the office.

The principal is now reviewing the school's phone policy and must choose between two options:

Policy 1: Allow students to bring phones to school and use them during lunch and other free periods.
Policy 2: Completely prohibit students from having phones at school.

I believe that students should not be permitted to bring phones to school for several important reasons.

First and foremost, students will inevitably use their phones to text message their friends during class lessons. Although some people argue that teenagers are mature enough to follow the rules and will not use their devices inappropriately, I strongly disagree with this viewpoint. While some students may be responsible, many others will simply ignore the instructions and use their phones anyway. It is unrealistic to expect all teenagers to exercise perfect self-control.

Additionally, phones can easily become a distraction for everyone in the classroom. Even if a student's phone is set to silent mode, there is always the possibility that it will ring or vibrate at an inappropriate moment. This disturbance affects not only the other students but also the teacher, who must stop the lesson to address the situation. The learning environment suffers as a result of these interruptions.

For these reasons, I am convinced that the school should adopt the second policy and prohibit phones entirely. This would create a calmer, more focused educational environment for all students.

Dear Principal,

I am writing to share my thoughts regarding your decision to improve the nutritional quality of our school meals, and I wish to express my strong support for this initiative.

First and foremost, this change addresses a serious concern that affects many students. A significant number of our classmates experience allergic reactions to certain ingredients in the current menu. As a result, many of them choose to skip meals entirely or go hungry throughout the school day. This situation is concerning because it could potentially lead to more severe health issues, including fainting episodes.

Furthermore, providing healthier food options will greatly benefit our cognitive performance. When students consume nutritious meals, our concentration and mental capabilities improve significantly. A balanced breakfast or a healthy lunch helps the brain function optimally, allowing us to participate more effectively in classroom activities from the very beginning of each lesson.

Additionally, nutritious food contains essential nutrients that support our physical development. Items such as carbohydrates, proteins, and healthy fats provide the energy we need for both academic and physical activities. These nutrients are vital for growth during these formative years.

Finally, introducing healthier meals may also encourage students who currently avoid school lunches to give them another chance. Many learners order food from external sources or bring meals from home because they either dislike the current offerings or cannot eat certain items due to allergies. If we improve the quality and variety of food available, more students might choose to eat in the cafeteria. This would also help the school reduce food waste and avoid financial losses.

In conclusion, I believe this is a wonderful and thoughtful decision that will benefit the entire student body. Thank you for taking the time to consider improvements that support our health and wellbeing.

In today's world, technology plays a crucial role in our daily lives, and its significance will only continue to grow in the years ahead. Humans have always sought improvements to make life more convenient and comfortable. While some individuals celebrate these advancements, others—including myself—believe that excessive reliance on technology negatively impacts our society. Specifically, I am concerned that people are gradually abandoning face-to-face interactions, children are spending less time outdoors and more time on gaming, and many individuals develop aggressive behavior when separated from their devices.

Looking back at how society functioned in previous generations, people frequently gathered in public spaces and engaged with one another directly. There was no instant messaging or video calls that could connect us with friends through a small screen. Unfortunately, this situation has transformed into a serious problem in contemporary society. Many individuals now prefer remaining indoors rather than going out to meet friends or simply appreciating their surroundings. They choose to communicate online with people they have never actually met. Some argue that conversing with strangers online presents no difference from speaking with strangers in person, but this perspective overlooks important dangers. When interacting with unknown individuals on the internet, there is always the risk that they are using false identities to steal personal information or engage in other malicious activities. In contrast, when people met strangers in the past, they could observe their behavior and actions directly. This was how friendships traditionally developed—through observing how someone conducted themselves. Today, however, the internet has become the primary method for making connections, yet we can never be certain whether these individuals are genuine.

When we reflect on childhood experiences, many of us remember enjoying outdoor activities: playing in the streets, visiting friends' homes, or spending time together at parks. However, the world has changed dramatically since those days. Modern technology has introduced video games, which have become incredibly popular among children and teenagers. The process is simple—connect a device to a television and begin playing. The problem arises when young people spend entire days gaming and refuse to participate in outdoor sports or visit friends. At school, conversations among students frequently center around video games, which can negatively impact their academic performance. Constant gaming prevents students from studying for important examinations or completing their assignments. When the first gaming consoles were originally invented, they represented an exciting innovation. However, not all children could afford them, so they would save their money for treats like ice cream or visits to amusement parks instead. In contrast, today's youth often show little interest in leaving their homes where their technology awaits.

Another concerning consequence of our increasing technological dependence involves behavioral changes. When individuals are prevented from using their devices, many become aggressive and violent. Families frequently experience conflicts when children react badly to restrictions on technology use. This phenomenon has become common worldwide. Some experts suggest that this reaction occurs because young people become immersed in virtual worlds where they can do whatever they please. When parents attempt to remove them from this "world" to encourage more normal behavior, the children resist strongly. Since technology has become ubiquitous in nearly every environment, breaking this habit has become extremely challenging. Even teenagers have been known to damage objects around them—including the gaming devices their parents purchased for them—when they become frustrated.

While some people argue that technology brings positive benefits by creating tools that simplify our lives, I maintain that these advancements are ultimately harmful. The excessive use of technology causes people to abandon natural social behaviors and seek convenience above all else. If we fail to regulate our dependence on these devices, the future of our society may suffer significant consequences.

I agree with Winston Churchill's famous observation about the significant role that failure plays in achieving success. This is because we need to learn how to maintain hope when working toward our goals and building our future. Consider this: what if you continue experiencing setback after setback, yet you remain confident that success will eventually come your way? What if you never lose faith or enthusiasm while pursuing your ambitions? This is precisely what the former British Prime Minister meant when he stated that "success consists of going from failure to failure without the loss of enthusiasm." But how can we know whether we are failing in our pursuit of success?

What does success actually mean? Success refers to accomplishing the goals we have set for ourselves. Every person desires to achieve something meaningful. Reaching success brings incredible satisfaction, but failure is something nobody enjoys, including those who have already found success. It is natural to make errors because they provide valuable learning opportunities, allowing us to try again until we succeed. Nobody is flawless, so making occasional mistakes is completely acceptable when we understand that we can grow from them.

You realize you are struggling to achieve success when you repeatedly make mistakes but continue moving forward until you eventually succeed. No matter how many times you stumble, this should not prevent you from pursuing what you truly want. You can still attain success regardless of how many failures you experience because each setback makes you wiser and better prepared for achievement.

Success is something many people have attained, while others have not. Ultimately, we are accountable for our mistakes, our actions, and our words, as they can impact others in various ways. As individuals, we must remain motivated to pursue success; otherwise, someone else will step forward and take the opportunity we let slip away.

I believe that every student should take part in at least one extracurricular activity, and I agree with the principal's decision to make this a requirement. There are many valuable reasons why participating in such activities is beneficial for young people both now and in the future.

First of all, getting involved in sports or other activities greatly improves physical health. Research has shown that students who participate in regular physical activities are less likely to develop health problems such as heart disease or breathing difficulties. Whether it is basketball, baseball, track and field, or even being part of a cheerleading squad, these activities help students stay active and maintain a healthy weight. Being physically active has numerous advantages that many people underestimate.

Beyond physical health, extracurricular activities also support emotional wellbeing. When students are engaged in something they enjoy, they get a break from their daily stresses and worries. This distraction provides relief from problems that may be bothering them. Additionally, these activities are not limited to sports alone. Students can also help with the school newspaper, assist counselors, work on the yearbook, or participate in community service. These opportunities allow young people to step outside their own concerns and focus on something positive.

Another important advantage is how extracurricular involvement helps with college applications. Universities are looking for well-rounded students, not just those with high grades. Participation in activities demonstrates responsibility, time management, and the ability to work with others. This can make a significant difference when applying for admission and scholarships. Colleges want to see that students can handle commitments and interact positively with their peers, as these skills are essential for success in higher education.

Finally, these activities encourage social interaction and help students build relationships. Rather than remaining isolated and self-focused, young people have the chance to connect with their classmates and form new friendships. This creates a more united school community where everyone feels included.

In conclusion, requiring students to participate in at least one extracurricular activity is a positive policy. It promotes better health, reduces stress, improves college prospects, and develops important social skills. Trying something new never hurts, and students may discover talents and interests they never knew they had.

Music, drama, and art classes are typically offered as elective courses. These subjects are not typically used in everyday life, and they are not necessary for graduation. There are many other alternatives that could replace them in the curriculum. Therefore, these subjects should not be mandatory for students to take, since each individual has their own aspirations and career goals.

In real life, we rely on practical skills such as basic mathematics to handle taxes and bills. However, when will we ever need music, drama, or art in our daily routines? These subjects are more like hobbies rather than essential skills needed for maintaining a stable life. Most employers do not care whether you can write a song, perform dramatically, or paint like the Mona Lisa. Including such skills in your resume will not help you secure a job in most fields. If you decide to specialize in these areas, only those who are exceptionally talented and skilled will achieve success. The majority of people will not be able to build a reliable career from these subjects.

Elective courses exist to help students explore potential career paths. If music, drama, and art became required subjects, it would be as if we were trying to create a second Renaissance era. These subjects are not considered important by colleges during the admissions process. Admissions officers focus more on prerequisite subjects and major requirements rather than artistic abilities. Your ability to paint or sculpt will not be evaluated on standardized tests like the SAT, which colleges use to determine eligibility.

As students grow older and pursue higher education, their career goals often change. For instance, someone might start college wanting to become a doctor but later decide to become a scientist instead. Fortunately, these two fields share similar foundational courses since both are science-related. However, subjects like music, drama, and art do not connect with other academic areas. They are specialized subjects that stand alone without overlapping with other disciplines.

While it is true that talented individuals can succeed in these fields by writing songs for famous artists, performing in plays and films, or gaining recognition for their artistic work, this is not realistic for most students. I can speak from my own experience on this matter. I used to be very shy and quiet. I would never approach people or start conversations because I felt uncomfortable around others. This transformation has made me much happier.

I did not want to be perceived negatively, so I worked on becoming more approachable and friendly. This positive change has greatly improved my life.

Those who claim that change is impossible are simply lacking in self-confidence. They do not believe in their own ability to grow and improve. I myself never imagined that I could become such a different person. In the past, I rarely smiled and was quite boring. Now, I am always smiling and much more lively.

I have also made the mistake of judging others too quickly based on first impressions. There were people I thought seemed uninteresting or unpleasant, but as I got to know them, I realized they were actually wonderful individuals. This proves that forming opinions too hastily is not a good practice.

In conclusion, I strongly disagree with the notion that people should be judged by their first impressions. Everyone deserves the chance to be understood for who they truly are, and everyone has the capacity to change for the better.

I strongly agree that art, drama, and music classes should be optional subjects rather than mandatory ones. These creative subjects simply do not contribute to our future success in the real world. What truly matters is learning skills that will help us secure good jobs, pay our bills, and cover essential expenses like electricity, food, gas, and water. Creative subjects do not teach us these practical life skills.

Most young people prefer spending their time on social media, playing video games, hanging out with friends, playing sports, or going to parties. They do not want to sit in a classroom with classmates who are passionate about creative activities. Students should not be forced to attend classes they genuinely dislike.

Additionally, requiring students to take these subjects could lead to poor grades and failures. When students are not interested in a subject, they often skip classes or refuse to participate actively. Some students simply do not have natural talent in art or drama, and being forced to take these courses would result in low grades. This seems unfair to students who struggle with creative tasks.

Music might be the most appealing of these subjects, but it still lacks practical value for future careers. These classes should remain optional, similar to how band programs operate in schools. Creative subjects are meant for students who genuinely enjoy them and have natural abilities in those areas. Therefore, schools should offer these as elective options rather than graduation requirements.

I disagree with adding an extra hour and a half to the school day. My first reason is that students already spend approximately eight hours at school, and by the end of the day, they feel exhausted. Adding more time would simply be overwhelming for both children and teenagers.

My second reason is that longer school hours would reduce the time available for childhood experiences. When students finally leave school, they are often too tired to enjoy recreational activities. By the time they finish their homework, it becomes dark outside, and parents are reluctant to let them go out.

This connects to my third point about homework. Students typically receive assignments almost every day, and completing them can take several hours. For instance, if a student finishes school at four o'clock but still has two to three hours of homework ahead, there is no opportunity to spend time with friends or engage in enjoyable activities. By the evening, it is too late and dark to go outside.

My fourth reason concerns appointments. If school ends at two forty-five and a doctor or dental appointment is scheduled for three o'clock, the extra hours would make it impossible to attend. While students might be allowed to leave early, this would result in missing valuable instructional time.

I understand that schools want to provide additional learning opportunities to help students succeed in life and secure good jobs. However, children and adults both need time for themselves outside of academic responsibilities. These are the reasons why I disagree with extending the school day.

Many people believe that taking classes online or at home is a better option for students. I agree with this viewpoint because learners can focus more easily and achieve better results without distractions from others. When students study at home, nothing interrupts their concentration, allowing them to understand their lessons more deeply.

Some even sleep while the teacher is explaining important material. Consequently, these students may fail their exams and quizzes because they did not pay attention throughout the year.

On the other hand, students who study online or at home work independently and stay focused on their tasks. They develop better study habits and take more responsibility for their learning. When it comes to important tests at the end of the year, these students tend to perform better because they were actually listening and learning rather than socializing.

However, there is one advantage to attending regular school. Students have the opportunity to meet new people and make friends. This social aspect can be valuable because friends can support each other during difficult times. Despite this benefit, the primary goal of education is to learn, and online or home-based study proves more effective for achieving academic success.

In conclusion, studying online or at home offers significant advantages. Students can concentrate better, learn more material, and perform better on assessments. While traditional schooling provides social opportunities, the academic benefits of learning from home make it the superior choice for those who are serious about their education.
